message.content:
Owner request: research how Nxeon can become the best home for running AI agents (OpenClaw and its relatives, Grok-based bots, and other agent runtimes), figure out how to support them seamlessly, and build a beautiful animated marketing page featuring the agents and their avatars. Notes to /root/agent-notes/agents-marketing.md as you go; research report to /root/research/agents-support.md; final report at the end.

HARD RULES: read /root/agent-briefs/growth-batch-2026-10-02.md first, all its rules apply (no prod DB writes, no node/VM changes, no secrets in logs, explicit-path commits, never `git add -A`, no builds in /opt/nxeon or on the primary's live tree: use a git worktree on /tank off main e.g. `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/nxeon-wt-agents -b feature/ai-agents-hosting main`, cp -a node_modules, dummy DATABASE_URL for prisma generate, the heavy lock at /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/heavy.sh). Do NOT deploy, do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch the live marketing site. Nxeon speaks as the owner: never imply a third-party infrastructure provider exists. Never fabricate stats, testimonials, customer counts, benchmarks, endorsements or partnerships. The '47 seconds' tagline is an intentional brand line. Third-party names and logos (OpenClaw, xAI/Grok, Claude, others) are trademarks: refer to them nominatively and factually ('runs OpenClaw'), no implied endorsement, and draw ORIGINAL avatars, never copy an official logo or mascot artwork.

READ FIRST for brand and conventions: memory-style facts: the real brand theme is navy + violet + cyan (gradient blue #3b6be8 to violet #7b3fef, a placeholder magenta #e5197e is the third stop), not charcoal/amber; the owner has rejected generic templated layouts and mockups that drift off-theme, so work from the LITERAL existing site files and iterate with REAL screenshots (Playwright) compared against the existing marketing pages until yours is clearly the same design language but more distinctive. Study the new marketing site (NXM_ROOT middleware switch, tools/nxm generators, app/nxm/, components/marketing/), the existing game pages (components/marketing/gamelanding) and the design docs in docs/ (NEXION-V2.md, DOCUMENTATION.md marketing sections), /root/research/*.md, and the brand assets library (owner's PNG art in board-uploads, find by alpha scan; reuse before creating).

PART 1, RESEARCH (use WebSearch/WebFetch, cite sources, no guessing): (a) what OpenClaw is (the open-source always-on personal AI agent that runs on a user's machine or server, formerly ClawdBot/Moltbot; verify the history and current name), how people deploy it, its resource needs, channels (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack), model backends, security concerns (it executes tools and shell on the host, so isolation matters), common failure modes; (b) Grok bots: how people run xAI Grok API bots (Telegram/Discord/X), the xAI API, typical hosting needs; (c) other agent runtimes people self-host (Hermes agents, AutoGPT-style, n8n, LangGraph/CrewAI services, MCP servers, Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code headless, browser agents) and what they need from a host: always-on VM, persistent disk, outbound egress, secrets storage, webhooks and inbound HTTPS, scheduled jobs, GPU optional, snapshots, budgets; (d) what competitors offer for agent hosting (be factual; note pricing only if verified from their pages); (e) what Nxeon already has that fits (VPS plans, one-click apps, Docker templates, API keys, partner API, SSH key injection, wallet/credits, firewall, backups, Claude template? grep lib/ for 'claude', worker/claude.ts, one-click apps) and the gaps.

PART 2, THE SUPPORT PLAN (docs, not code yet): a concrete, phased roadmap to make this seamless: (1) one-click 'AI agent' VPS templates with the runtime preinstalled and hardened (OpenClaw, a generic Grok bot starter, MCP server host, n8n), including recommended plans and RAM sizes, (2) an agent-friendly control plane so an AGENT can self-provision and manage its own server safely: scoped API tokens, an OpenAPI spec, an MCP server for Nxeon, a CLI, programmatic checkout with spend caps and a wallet budget, llms.txt, SSH key injection, webhooks, (3) safety defaults: isolated VM, egress rules, no root by default, secret storage, resource caps, abuse controls, (4) onboarding flow and docs, (5) pricing/packaging suggestion (clearly marked as a suggestion for the owner), (6) effort estimate per phase, what can ship fast, what needs owner decisions. Include a risk section (abuse, runaway spend, prompt-injection to host compromise).

PART 3, THE MARKETING PAGE (build it for real in the worktree, not deployed): a beautiful, animated, on-brand page at an agreed route inside the marketing site (follow the NXM structure; pick the route, e.g. /ai-agents) featuring an avatar cast of original animated SVG/CSS characters, one per agent family (an OpenClaw-style claw character, a Grok-style bot character, a Claude-style character, a generic MCP/n8n helper, etc., all ORIGINAL and clearly stylized, each with idle animation, a hover reaction and a small speech bubble), a hero where agents 'come online' on an Nxeon server (a live-feeling terminal or status strip, using clearly illustrative, honestly labelled sample content), a how-it-works strip (pick template, deploy in seconds, agent online), template cards, safety/isolation section, an 'agents can set themselves up' section describing the planned API/MCP honestly as 'coming' where it is not built, FAQ, and CTAs into the existing deploy wizard. Animations: scroll-triggered reveals, avatar idle loops, a flowing connection-line graphic, subtle parallax; respect prefers-reduced-motion; keep it fast (no heavy libraries, CSS/SVG/vanilla or what the repo already uses); fully responsive; accessible (alt text, focus states, contrast). Do not claim features that do not exist; label planned ones 'Coming soon'. Take real Playwright screenshots at desktop and mobile widths, and iterate against the existing site until it is polished. Provide the screenshots in /root/agent-notes/agents-marketing/ and a way to preview locally on a free port (not 3000/3001/3010/3020/3021).

FINAL REPORT: key research findings with sources, the support plan summary, the branch and commits, the page route and files, screenshot paths and preview command, what is placeholder, what claims you avoided, and the owner decisions needed. tsc --noEmit must be 0 errors and tests green before reporting.

- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: Always use this skill when the user wants to create a new Figma Design, FigJam, or Slides file. You MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call.
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. - figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-generative-plugins: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_generative_plugin` or `update_generative_plugin`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or extend a reusable generative Figma plugin.

Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-shaders: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_shader` or `update_shader`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or iterate on a shader effect, shader fill, custom effect, custom fill, or procedural shader in Figma.

Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. # Growth batch brief — Nxeon, 2026-10-02 (applies to every agent in this batch)

## Source of truth for your items
- Owner decisions: /root/growth/decisions-summary.json (`dec` map; `do` / `change` = approved, `skip` = do NOT build).
- Full item write-ups (title, rationale, evidence, effort): /root/growth/*.json and the matching *.md files (marketing-acquisition, product-growth, seo-content, ops). Read the item text for your ids before building; follow its stated approach and honour its caveats.
- Prior art and rules: /root/FLEET-STATUS-2026-10-01.md, /root/agent-notes/*.md, repo CLAUDE.md, docs/DOCUMENTATION.md.

## Hard rules (violating any of these is a failure)
1. Never edit, build, test or restart inside /opt/nxeon. Work ONLY in your own git worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-<name> -b <branch> main`. main already contains the day's fixes; branch from current main.
2. In the worktree, node_modules and .prisma/@prisma must be REAL copies, never symlinks (see /root/agent-notes/provfix.md). Never run `prisma generate` against /opt/nxeon's client. Use a throwaway Postgres for anything DB-related.
3. Take the box-wide heavy lock for builds and test runs: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/heavy.sh (the box is shared by ~7 agents; do not run more than one heavy command at a time).
4. Commit with explicit paths only (`git add <paths>`), never `git add -A`. Do not push. Notes go to /root/agent-notes/<name>.md.
5. You must not touch production, any Proxmox node, any VM, any customer data, any email/SMS/Discord/social send, any payment or card action, or any paid third-party tool. Everything that sends, charges or posts must be built behind a default-OFF flag or produced as a draft for the owner. Do not deploy; the owner's session merges and promotes.
6. Schema changes must be purely additive (the production deploy only runs additive `prisma db push`).
7. Honesty: never fabricate statistics, reviews, customer counts, awards or testimonials. Claims must come from real data in the repo/DB or be omitted. The "47 seconds" tagline is intentional brand copy; never flag or change it. Never mention a third-party infrastructure provider to customers; Nxeon speaks as the owner. Customer-visible copy: no "provider".
8. Brand: use existing design tokens/components (navy + violet + cyan; brand gradient blue→violet→magenta). Match surrounding code style, naming and comment density. Update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md for operational/third-party knowledge.
9. Money path (checkout, pricing, billing, Stripe, wallet): extra care. Build behind flags, add tests, and state exactly what was and was not verified. Never run a live charge.
10. Legal flags: Hytale and FiveM are legally sensitive (owner decision: no managed FiveM sale without permission). Content for these is informational only, and you must say so in your notes.
11. No overlap: stay inside your assigned item ids. If you need a file another agent owns, make the smallest possible change and say so in your notes.
12. Verify before reporting: run typecheck and the tests related to your change, and run what you can locally (a local dev render is fine if it uses a throwaway DB; never the shared prod DB). Your final report must list: branch, commits, files touched, what you verified, what you could not verify, any owner decisions or owner actions needed, and any flags/env vars to enable.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. Only the page itself is wrapped in a document skeleton at publish time: an HTML file in `files` is another page served without one, so Claude starts each with its own `<!doctype html>`, charset and viewport metas and base styles, or, without the doctype, it renders in quirks mode with browser defaults. favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

**LIVE IN PRODUCTION since 2026-09-27** (release/nxm-launch fast-forwarded into main at 49aa21912a, promoted by me on the owner's go). The code still lives under app/nxm; `NXM_ROOT=1` in /opt/nxeon/.env makes middleware.ts rewrite every URL in app/nxm/_data/live-routes.json (regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/nxm-live-routes.ts` after adding a page) to app/nxm and 301 /nxm/* to the real URL; `NXM_LIVE=1` = indexable. ROLLBACK: remove both flags from /opt/nxeon/.env + `systemctl restart nxeon-web` — the old app/(marketing) pages take over, untouched. Staging also has NXM_ROOT=1. New marketing work now branches from main (feature/marketing-nxm is merged). Launch also shipped: custom-server builder, wizard popularity tracking (/admin/popularity), VPS system logs, a 72-hour money-back guarantee (lib/refund-policy.ts — Terms/card/comparisons/support KB all read it). NOT applied: the 4-tier game prices (prisma/seed-gameplans-4tier.ts, needs owner price sign-off).

(History) The new marketing site was built on branch `feature/marketing-nxm`, worktree /root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm.
- Deploy to staging with `scripts/deploy-staging.sh feature/marketing-nxm` (https://staging.nxeon.cloud/nxm). If someone deploys main to staging, /nxm disappears.
- Everything under /nxm 404s unless `NXEON_ENV=staging`, and the pages are noindex until `NXM_LIVE=1`.

How it's built (full guide in tools/nxm/README.md on the branch):
- Generators: `tools/nxm/port_home.py` builds the homepage and `tools/nxm/port_pages.py` builds every other page. The latter runs the design package's own builders, intercepting only the base64/dist-write step. Edit the scripts, never their outputs.
- Real data: wire modules (`tools/nxm/wire/<slug>.py`) put `{{nxm:key}}` slots and `__NXM` constants into the page, and loaders (`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`) fill them from the system at request time.
  - The porter's audit must say `wired` or `static` with no stale prices for every page.
  - The owner requires that nothing is hardcoded.
- SEO: registry `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (seeded from live) plus `meta(p)`, `nxmMetadata`, and auto Breadcrumb/FAQ JSON-LD plus loader JSON-LD.
- Native pages (not in the design package) live in `tools/nxm/native/<slug>`. Examples: about, security, affiliate, legal (legal text moved to lib/legal, shared with the live pages).

Gotchas learned:
- Never scope CSS with `:root:has()` (causes whole-page restyle storms).
- The design's `<body class/style/data-*>` must ride on the page wrapper.
- The dev server grows to 11 GB on this production box: restart it with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`.
- Parallel agents in one worktree: commit only explicit paths.
- Render ported markup only through `StableHtml` (app/nxm/_components). React 19 re-sets innerHTML whenever the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` object changes identity, even for an identical string. The promo popup's server action sets a cookie on a first visit, which refreshes the route and used to wipe the page script's work on every page.
- Design class names collide with Tailwind/global utilities (`.ring`, `.container`, `.grid`, `.dot`, `.chip`…). The `:where()` resets at the end of nxm.css handle this, so check there first for any mystery border, box or size.

Related branches (the owner promotes them):
- `fix/portal-root-class`: portal CSS `:root.nx-portal`.
- `feat/deploy-wizard-tweaks`: no discount badges, real latency (Falkenstein needs a ping endpoint on node-2), "Use a different card", standard deploy button.

**Regions (owner, 2026-09-27): "we plan on adding all of these regions, so stop removing them."** Keep every region/location the design or live pages show (globe, maps, counts, location pages). Only deploy/checkout links are limited to enabled nodes. A region change must never make a page throw — warn and keep rendering.

Open owner decisions (asked 2026-09-27):
- Renewal promise vs intro prices.
- Terms jurisdiction placeholder.

Answered: keep homepage claims (Shield vendors, CLI/API, Samsung NVMe, Modrinth/mod.io); mention the Creator Partner Program on /affiliate as a limited-time launch offer.

**Why:** the owner wants the site exactly as designed, plus their identity picks, wired to the real system. See [[nxeon-redesign-generic-drift]] and [[nxeon-marketing-redesign-2026-09]].

Use `grad-text` (blue→violet), `.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.eyebrow`, `hero-aura`, `tone-panel/deep/light`, `.rail`. Cyan is the in-theme "live/active" pop — NEVER amber (amber only as a semantic warning).
2. **Templated/boring layout.** Every version was the same skeleton: dark bg + a canvas particle animation + centered eyebrow → stacked sections → stat strip → product grid → pricing → CTA. That IS the "AI slop" they said they don't want. They want bolder, asymmetric, editorial composition.

**2026-08-02 VIDEO BRIEF (board "Website Overhaul" card, 4:51 narrated screen-rec — the authoritative direction).** The user compared THREE sources and wants them combined into a NEW preview version (built `/v8`): (1) a rocket.new AI prototype "Deploy anywhere. name: nxeon-build-isolation
description: "NEVER run npm run build (or agent builds) in the live prod tree /opt/nxeon — it clobbers prod's .next and breaks the site"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc
  modified: 2026-08-11T05:24:18.217Z
---

**NEVER run `npm run build` in the live prod working tree `/opt/nxeon`.** nxeon-web serves `/opt/nxeon/.next` and nxeon-worker runs `tsx worker/index.ts` off the same tree. A build there overwrites `.next` (new chunk hashes) while the OLD server process keeps running → browser requests chunks by hashes that no longer exist → `ChunkLoadError` / "Something went wrong" on every page (esp. /admin). Also `git checkout <branch>` in the prod tree switches the worker's live code.

**Why:** 2026-08-10 overnight run — I spawned build agents as normal general-purpose agents that `git checkout -b` + `npm run build` INSIDE /opt/nxeon. Each build clobbered prod's compiled assets; prod admin threw ChunkLoadError for hours. Fix was: stop the agent, `git checkout <last-promoted-commit>`, `npm run build`, `chown -R nxeon:nxeon .next`, `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`, then hard-refresh the browser.

**How to apply:** build/verify agents MUST work in an ISOLATED git worktree (Agent `isolation: "worktree"`, or manual `git worktree add`) or in `/opt/nxeon-staging` — NEVER the prod tree. The prod tree `/opt/nxeon` should stay parked at the currently-deployed commit; only `scripts/promote-production.sh` (build+restart) moves prod, and only on explicit user authorization. Staging builds go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` which operates on `/opt/nxeon-staging`. See [[nxeon-ventures-hub]], [[nxeon-platform]].

name: nxeon-worktree-nodemodules-hazard
description: "NEVER git add -A in a worktree that has a node_modules symlink — it can destroy prod's real node_modules"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc
  modified: 2026-08-21T17:19:08.560Z
---

On 2026-08-21 I nearly took prod down. In a worktree I created `node_modules` as a symlink to `/opt/nxeon/node_modules` (the standard setup), then ran `git add -A` which COMMITTED the symlink (`.gitignore` has `node_modules/` with a trailing slash, which does NOT match a symlink named `node_modules`). Fast-forwarding that commit into the prod tree `/opt/nxeon` replaced its **real** `node_modules` directory with a **self-referential symlink** (`/opt/nxeon/node_modules -> /opt/nxeon/node_modules`), deleting 1.1G of packages. `next` and the Prisma client became unresolvable; only the in-memory running services survived.

**Why:** never stage the whole tree in a symlinked worktree.
**How to apply:**
- In worktrees, `git add` ONLY the specific files you changed — never `git add -A` / `git add .`.
- Recovery if it happens: `git rm --cached node_modules && rm -f node_modules` in the prod tree, then `npm ci` (lockfile present) + `npx prisma generate`, then commit the untracking. Do this BEFORE any restart/promote — running services hold modules in memory but a build/restart will fail hard.
- Consider hardening `.gitignore` with a bare `node_modules` line (no slash) so the symlink is ignored too.

Relates to [[nxeon-build-isolation]] and the deploy flow in [[nxeon-resume-point]].

#!/bin/bash
# Two-slot lock so at most TWO heavy jobs (tsc, next dev, playwright, test suites) run at once on this box.
# This machine is the live production primary (also hosts customer VMs) — uncontrolled parallel tsc/dev servers
# can OOM or starve production. (Was 1 slot; raised to 2 on 2026-10-01 because 20 agents were queueing.)
# usage: heavy.sh bash -c "cd /opt/nxeon-wt-foo && npx tsc --noEmit -p ."
deadline=$((SECONDS + 3600))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ]; do
  for i in 1 2; do
    exec {fd}>/tmp/nxeon-heavy.$i.lock
    if flock -n $fd; then
      exec nice -n 19 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=3072" "$@"
    fi
    exec {fd}>&-
  done
  sleep 2
done
echo "heavy.sh: timed out waiting for a slot" >&2; exit 75

# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

Do I need to install Claude Code myself?

No. Every new Nxeon VPS ships with Claude Code pre-installed at first boot. If you’re on a server from before this shipped, one command adds it (shown in your dashboard). There’s no reinstall or rebuild involved.

Is there a separate “vibe coding” plan or price?

No. This runs on the same VPS plans sold on /vps: there’s no AI-hosting markup or separate tier. Pick the plan that fits your workload; Claude Code is included at every level.

How do I pay for Claude usage?

You bring your own Claude subscription (Pro or Max) or an Anthropic API key. Claude Code asks which the first time you run it. Either way, that’s billed by Anthropic directly and is separate from your Nxeon invoice.

Can I use Claude Code on my own computer instead?

Yes, it’s the same Claude Code either way. Running it on a Nxeon VPS mainly buys you a server that doesn’t sleep when your laptop does, so long builds and always-on apps keep running.

Does it deploy to a domain automatically?

Claude runs and previews your app on your server. Pointing your own domain at it is a normal DNS step you do yourself. There’s no automatic subdomain or certificate wizard bundled with this.

"""Shared transforms for porting the design package into app/nxm.

Used by port_pages.py (every inner page) and port_home.py (links only). Each
transform applies one of the owner's identity decisions
(/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/IDENTITY-SPEC.md) to the package's own markup/CSS/JS.
"""
import json, os, re

PKG = "/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff"
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

# The new site lives under BASE on staging until launch; at launch BASE becomes "".
BASE = "/nxm"

# package slug -> production route (docs/url-map.json, with the TBD routes decided)
ROUTES = {
    "home": "/",
    "matrix": "/matrix",
    "pricing": "/pricing",
    "compare": "/compare",
    "vps-vs-digitalocean": "/vps-vs-digitalocean",
    "vps": "/vps",
    "web-hosting": "/web-hosting",
    "business-email": "/business-email",
    "domains": "/domains",
    "migrate": "/migrate",
    "nxcloud": "/nxcloud",
    "free-vps": "/free-vps",
    "free-minecraft": "/free-minecraft",
    "game-servers": "/game-servers",
    "minecraft-server-hosting": "/minecraft-server-hosting",
    "minecraft-server-hosting-singapore": "/minecraft-server-hosting/singapore",
    "singapore-vps-hosting": "/singapore-vps-hosting",
    "germany-vps-hosting": "/germany-vps-hosting",
    "wordpress-vps-hosting": "/wordpress-vps-hosting",
    "docker-hosting": "/docker-hosting",
    "nxlabs": "/mods",
    "mods-minecraft": "/mods/games/[family]",
    "mods-minecraft-browse": "/mods/games/[family]/all",
    "mod-lithium": "/mods/[family]/[slug]",
    "game-servers-mods": "/game-servers/mods",  # native: mod support on game servers
    "blog": "/blog",
    "blog-vaultwarden-nginx": "/blog/[slug]",
    "contact": "/contact",
    # native pages (tools/nxm/native/<slug>), fanned out by tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json
    "legal": "/legal/terms",
    "about": "/about",
    "security": "/security",
    "affiliate": "/affiliate",
    # the design's use-case page (source/pages/_use) for 4 apps + 4 VPS landers (routes/use-case.json)
    "use-case": "/n8n-hosting",
    # the design's /migrate page told per host: 10 routes (routes/migrate-from.json);
    # "vps-vs-digitalocean" above is the comparison template, 16 routes (routes/vps-vs-digitalocean.json)
    "migrate-from": "/migrate-from-digitalocean",
    "developers": "/developers",
    "features": "/features",
    "vibe-coding": "/vibe-coding",
    "block-storage": "/block-storage",
    "status": "/status",
    "help": "/help",
    "docs": "/docs",
    "tools": "/tools",
    "tools-tool": "/tools/domain-generator",  # fan-out: tools/nxm/routes/tools-tool.json
    # the location template: EVERY generated location landing (~770 slugs from
    # lib/marketing/*Landings.ts) is served by ONE hand-written dynamic route,
    # app/nxm/[slug]/page.tsx (routes/location-landing.json is [] so the port
    # writes no route file); the example here is one concrete slug so
    # _is_ported never matches every single-segment path
    "location-landing": "/london-vps-hosting",
    # public server directory (native): /servers + /game-servers/directory (routes/server-directory.json)
    "server-directory": "/servers",
    "server-detail": "/servers/[subdomain]",
    # Nxeon community server (native; 404s unless a FreePublicServer row is LIVE)
    "free-valheim-server": "/free-valheim-server",
    # Nxeon Verified mod badge explainer (native, pure copy)
    "mods-verified": "/mods/verified",
}
# Template routes ([params]) are served for every item; links in the design
# that pointed at the example item keep pointing at that concrete item.
EXAMPLES = {
    "mods-minecraft": "/mods/games/minecraft",
    "mods-minecraft-browse": "/mods/games/minecraft/all",
    "mod-lithium": "/mods/minecraft/lithium",
    "blog-vaultwarden-nginx": "/blog/how-to-self-host-vaultwarden-behind-an-nginx-reverse-proxy",
}
def _is_ported(path):
    for r in ROUTES.values():
        if re.fullmatch(re.sub(r"\\\[\w+\\\]", r"[^/]+", re.escape(r)), path):
            return True
    return False
PORTED = set(ROUTES.values())
# fanned-out template routes (tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json) are ported too
import glob as _glob
for _f in _glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "routes", "*.json")):
    PORTED |= {e["route"] for e in json.load(open(_f))}

def staged(route: str) -> str:
    """Where a production route lives right now: inside BASE when ported."""
    path = re.split(r"[?#]", route, 1)[0] or "/"
    rest = route[len(path):] if route.startswith(path) else ""
    if path in PORTED or _is_ported(path):
        return (BASE + ("" if path == "/" else path) or "/") + rest
    return route

# preview URL -> production route
_umap = json.load(open(f"{PKG}/docs/url-map.json"))
PREVIEW = {}
for k, v in _umap.items():
    if not k.startswith("http"):
        continue
    v = v.split(" ")[0]
    PREVIEW[k] = v if v.startswith("/") else "#"
# the package's TBD routes, decided
PREVIEW["https://claude.ai/artifact/4YHjiNW6XfAZdbvfSscmL9"] = ROUTES["nxcloud"]
PREVIEW["https://claude.ai/artifact/VudtGnVtYxp9VFFwSrc5p9"] = ROUTES["minecraft-server-hosting-singapore"]
PREVIEW["https://claude.ai/artifact/Aa86KqSASP24hJrS537TxJ"] = "/minecraft-server-hosting/germany"  # a game x location fan-out route
PREVIEW["https://claude.ai/artifact/DrDRgobmxKJbiDHMW9GwkL"] = EXAMPLES["mods-minecraft-browse"]
for _k, _v in list(PREVIEW.items()):
    for _slug, _ex in EXAMPLES.items():
        if _v == ROUTES[_slug]:
            PREVIEW[_k] = _ex

def relink(s: str) -> str:
    """Preview URLs -> routes; nxeon.cloud absolute links -> relative; routes
    that are already ported point inside BASE so staging stays on the new site."""
    def prev(m):
        route = PREVIEW.get(m.group(1), "#")
        return staged(route + (m.group(2) or "")) if route != "#" else "#"
    s = re.sub(r"(https://claude\.ai/artifact/[A-Za-z0-9]+)([?#][^\"'\s)`]*)?", prev, s)
    s = re.sub(r"https://nxeon\.cloud(/[^\"'\s)`<]*)?", lambda m: staged(m.group(1) or "/"), s)
    finally:
        builtins.open, base64.b64encode = real_open, real_b64
        os.chdir(cwd)
    html = next(v for k, v in cap.items() if k.startswith("nxeon-"))
    return html

# ── native pages: pages the design package doesn't include ─────────────────
# Authored in the package's own page format (body.html with {{SPRITE}}/{{NAV}}/
# {{FOOTER}}, page.css, page.js, meta.json) under tools/nxm/native/<slug>/ and
# assembled exactly like the package's build_page.py: shared shell + common.css
# + aurora + the page's own css/js. Then the same pipeline as every page.
NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native"
def build_native(slug):
    D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/"
    meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json"))
    p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3))
    MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs"
    head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{meta['title']}</title>", p1, count=1)
    head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
    head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none")
    css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "")
    head = head.replace("</style>", css + "</style>", 1)
    sprite = p2[p2.index("<body>") + 6:p2.index("</svg>") + 6]
    local = set(meta.get("anchors", []))
    def fix_links(h):
        h = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith("i-")) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', h)
        return h.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
    nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index("</header>") + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
    nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
    footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index("</footer>") + 9])
    body = open(D + "body.html").read()
    for k, v in {"SPRITE": sprite, "NAV": nav, "FOOTER": footer, "MAIN": MAIN}.items():
        body = body.replace("{{" + k + "}}", v)
    helpers = p3[p3.index("<script>"):p3.index("/* ------------------------------------------------------------------")]
    def blk(a, b): i = p3.index(a); j = p3.index(b, i + len(a)); return p3[i:j]
    js = helpers + "document.getElementById('year') && (document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear());\n"
    js += blk("/* ============ Navigation ============ */", "/* ============ Reveal, rules")
    js += blk("/* ============ Reveal, rules, in-view hooks, counters ============ */", "/* ============ Hero: Power Your")
    js += AURORA_JS + "\n" + (open(D + "page.js").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.js") else "") + "\n})();\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"
    html = head + body + js
    A = f"{PKG}/assets/"
    m = {k: (v if v.startswith("/") else A + v) for k, v in meta.get("assets", {}).items()}
    m.setdefault("LOGO", A + "logo.png")
    for _k in ["minecraft", "rust", "palworld", "valheim", "ark", "cs2"]:
        m.setdefault("NAV_" + _k.upper(), A + "nav/" + _k + ".webp")
    mime = lambda q: "image/png" if q.endswith(".png") else "image/svg+xml" if q.endswith(".svg") else "image/jpeg" if q.endswith(".jpg") else "image/webp"
    for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True):
        html = html.replace(f"__IMG_{k}__", f"data:{mime(m[k])};base64," + _fake_b64(open(m[k], "rb").read()).decode())
    left = set(re.findall(r"__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__", html)); assert not left, left
    return html

EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"}
def externalise(s):
    def rep(m):
        h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin")
        path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h])
        return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}"
    s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s)
    assert "NXMA" not in s
    return s

AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read()
AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read()

def port(slug):
    html = externalise(build_native(slug) if os.path.isdir(f"{NATIVE}/{slug}") else build(slug))
    head, rest = html.split("</head>", 1)
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", head).group(1)
    desc_m = re.search(r'<meta name="description" content="([^"]*)"', head)
    desc = desc_m.group(1) if desc_m else ""

    # CSS: the page's one stylesheet minus Aurora (already loaded, scoped, by
    # app/nxm/layout.tsx), scoped under this page's wrapper.
    css = re.search(r"<style>([\s\S]*)</style>", head).group(1)
    assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim"
    css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, ""))
    scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root"
    # the design's <body …>: its classes, CSS variables and data-* move to the
    # page wrapper (a nested page can't touch <body>); `xray` is a class the
    # design's JS toggles on body
    btag = re.search(r"<body([^>]*)>", html).group(1)
    battr = lambda n: (re.search(rf'{n}="([^"]*)"', btag) or [None, ""])[1]
    bclasses = battr("class").split()
    body_attrs = {"cls": " ".join(bclasses), "style": battr("style"),
                  "data": {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'data-([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', btag)}}
    hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls, frozenset(bclasses) | {"xray"})
    extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n"
             f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n"
             f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n")
    css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n"
               + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra)

    # Markup: everything between <body> and the page script.
    js_at = rest.rfind("<script>")
    body, js = rest[:js_at], rest[js_at:]
    body = re.sub(r"^\s*<body[^>]*>", "", body.strip())
    body = relink(body)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        assert old in body, (slug, old); body = body.replace(old, new)
    body, btns = swap_buttons(body)
    body, nrev = reviews_slot(body)
    body, ncta, nlogin, npost = nav_slots(body)
    assert ncta == 2 and nlogin == 2 and npost == 1, (slug, ncta, nlogin, npost)
    body, nfoot = re.subn(r'<footer class="footer"[\s\S]*?</footer>', "", body)
    assert nfoot == 1, (slug, nfoot)
    body = re.sub(r"<!--(?!NXM:)[\s\S]*?-->", "", body)
    stray = balanced(body)
    assert not stray, f"{slug}: stray end tags {stray[:3]}"
    wire = load_wire(slug)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "body"):
        body = wire.body(body)

    # Script: the page's JS minus the Aurora runtime (mounted once by the layout).
    js = re.search(r"<script>([\s\S]*)</script>", js).group(1)
    assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim"
    js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "")

When Nxeon design work needs premium imagery, look in `/opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/*/`
BEFORE scraping stock. The owner uploads brand art there and it is already licensed
to them, on-palette, and transparent — strictly better than anything free stock
gives, and it needs no "replace before production" caveat.

The uploads are mostly screenshots, so find the art by transparency: PNGs in
RGBA mode whose alpha histogram is >18% near-zero are cut-outs, not screenshots.
That one filter found the whole set in a single pass (~18 hits out of thousands).

What is in there (2026-09-06): the glowing N mark, an isometric neon server
stack, a neon database, two globes (full sphere + Earth's limb with arcs), the
brand light-ribbon wave, a gamepad, a 5-up service-icon strip, a 7-badge rank
pack (Bronze->Apex), and grids of UI/app-logo marks. Extracted into
`/opt/nxeon-v2/public/nx/art/` and `public/nx/ranks/` with a README recording
provenance; `tools/badges.py` re-slices the rank pack.

**Slicing an icon sheet, both mistakes I made:** columns are NOT evenly spaced
(the badges widen Bronze->Apex) — detect them from alpha column-sums. And a
square crop centred on a wide badge reaches down into its label pill — crop
tight to the body first, then pad to square.

For backdrop plates where no owner asset fits, NASA image releases are public
domain (17 U.S.C. §105) and safe for production; gradient-map their luminance
onto the Nexion ramp to fix the palette (real auroras are green, nebulae are
orange). Recipe in `/opt/nxeon-v2/tools/plates.py`. Unsplash comps under
`public/nx/placeholder/` are NOT cleared — those still need replacing.

Based on the search results, here's information about self-hosted n8n Docker installation with the `n8n_data` volume and `WEBHOOK_URL` requirements:

## n8n_data Volume

The n8n_data subdirectory stores n8n's persistent data, and mounting a host directory like ./n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n persists workflows, credentials, and execution data outside the container, ensuring your data survives updates, restarts, or container recreation.

The typical Docker volume setup is:
- Create the volume with `docker volume create n8n_data` and mount it as `-v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n`

## WEBHOOK_URL Requirements

WEBHOOK_URL sets the public URL for webhooks, which is important if you use HTTPS or a custom domain. 

n8n needs to know its own public HTTPS address so the URLs it hands to external services (for triggers and callbacks) actually reach it. Additionally, WEBHOOK_URL should use the public HTTPS origin, and N8N_PROXY_HOPS should match the reverse proxy chain if behind a proxy.

Example configuration:
```yaml
environment:
  - WEBHOOK_URL=https://n8n.yourdomain.com/
volumes:
  - n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n
```

# OpenClaw Installation Requirements & Methods

## Node.js Version Requirement
"Node 24.16+ or 26.1+" is required, with Node 26 being the recommended version.

## Quick Install Commands

**macOS/Linux/WSL2:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Alternative Installation Methods

1. **Desktop Apps**: Windows Hub installer or macOS DMG available from GitHub releases
2. **Local Prefix**: `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh | bash`
3. **Package Managers**: npm, pnpm, or bun with global installation flags
4. **From Source**: Git clone with pnpm build workflow
5. **Container Options**: Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, or Nix deployment

## System Requirements

The platform supports "macOS, Linux, or Windows" environments. Windows users have native Hub app and PowerShell installer options, while others can use shell scripts or container deployments.

## Post-Installation Verification

Run `openclaw --version`, `openclaw doctor`, and `openclaw gateway status` to confirm successful installation and proper configuration.

# Running OpenClaw on a VPS: Key Guidance

**Gateway Binding & Access:**
The documentation recommends: "keep the Gateway on loopback and access it via SSH tunnel or Tailscale Serve." When binding to broader networks, the Gateway requires authentication credentials unless a trusted proxy handles auth.

**State & Backups:**
"Treat the VPS as the source of truth and back up the state + workspace regularly." The Gateway owns both application state and workspace data on the VPS instance.

**Security Approach:**
Before deploying to a public VPS, harden administrative access first. Using Tailscale provides a secure path—join the VPS to your tailnet, verify SSH access works over that connection, then restrict public SSH exposure.

**Team Usage:**
For shared team agents, keep the runtime on dedicated infrastructure and OS user accounts. Avoid signing the runtime into personal accounts or profiles to maintain proper trust boundaries.

**Architecture:**
Users connect remotely via the Control UI or SSH/Tailscale tunnels, while the VPS serves as the source-of-truth runtime. Optionally, nodes on local devices can provide screen/camera capabilities while the Gateway remains cloud-hosted.

**Performance Notes:**
For low-power VMs or ARM hosts, enable Node's module compile cache and set `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1` to reduce startup overhead and simplify process management.

# Nxeon as the home for AI agents: research + support plan

Date: 2026-10-04. Author: agents-marketing agent. Branch: `feature/ai-agents-hosting` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-agents`).
Status: research and plan only. Nothing here is built except the marketing page (Part 3). Every external claim has a source.
Tags: **[V]** means the primary page was read on 2026-10-04. **[S]** means a secondary source or search snippet. **unverified** means it could not be confirmed and must not be used as a claim.

Raw research notes, with more links, are in the scratchpad file `agents-research-raw.md`.

---

## Part 1. Research

### (a) OpenClaw

**What it is.** OpenClaw is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed autonomous AI agent. It does tasks through LLMs and uses messaging apps as its main interface [V] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenClaw. The repo is https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw (TypeScript and Swift). The GitHub page showed 391k+ stars on 2026-10-04 [V].

**Name history** [V Wikipedia]:

| Date | Name |
|---|---|
| 2025-11-24 | Warelay |
| 2025-12-03 | CLAWDIS |
| 2026-01-02 | Clawdbot |
| 2026-01-27 | Moltbot, after Anthropic trademark complaints |
| 2026-01-30 | OpenClaw |

- The creator is Peter Steinberger. On 2026-02-14 he announced he was joining OpenAI and that an OpenClaw Foundation would steward the project [V Wikipedia].
- Some secondary sources say "Clawdbot" was the first public name [S]. Wikipedia's more granular timeline is used here.
- The current name is **OpenClaw**. The latest versions referenced are "OpenClaw 2.0 (v2026.8.1)" on 2026-08-30 (Wikipedia), and DigitalOcean ships 2026.9.3 [V].

**How people deploy it:**
- **Install.** `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`, or npm/pnpm/bun, from source, or Docker/Podman/Kubernetes/Nix.

  - "Treat the VPS as the source of truth and back up the state + workspace regularly".

  - Low-power VMs: enable the Node compile cache and set `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`.

- **Resource needs.** The docs read give **no official numeric minimum** (unverified).
  - DigitalOcean's catalogue recommends 4 GB / 2 CPU for personal use (1-5 users), 8 GB / 4 CPU for a small team, and 16 GB / 8 CPU for a medium team [V] https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/catalog/openclaw/.
  - Secondary guides say a text-only gateway is fine on about 4 GB and Chromium browser automation adds 2-4 GB [S] (sfailabs, psychz guides).
- **Channels.** WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal, iMessage and Teams, plus 20+ more [V repo].

  - A skill is a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter.

**Security** (why isolation matters):
- **Official hardening** [V] https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security:
  - loopback by default
  - DM pairing codes for unknown senders
  - group allowlists
  - "one trust boundary per gateway" (not for adversarial multi-tenant use)

- **Internet exposure:**
  - Censys saw about 1,000 rising to 21,000+ publicly exposed instances in under a week in late January 2026 [V] https://censys.com/blog/openclaw-in-the-wild-mapping-the-public-exposure-of-a-viral-ai-assistant/.
