- **Moltbook.** The agent-only social network built on OpenClaw exposed 1.5M API tokens [V] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moltbook.

**Common failure modes:**

**Relatives:**

- **How people run Grok bots.** The pattern:

| **n8n** | workflow automation, self-hosted via Docker | persistent `/home/node/.n8n` volume (holds the credential encryption key), a public HTTPS webhook URL, Postgres for production; about 2 vCPU / 2-4 GB [S] (n8n's own docs pages 404'd for us; official path docs.n8n.io/hosting/installation/docker/) |
| **LangGraph** (self-hosted Agent Server) | Postgres for checkpoints, Redis for pub/sub, a license key [S/docs] https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/deploy-standalone-server | Postgres, Redis, inbound HTTPS |
| **CrewAI / AutoGPT platform** | not verified (AutoGPT self-host guide: https://agpt.co/docs/platform/getting-started) | unverified; do not claim |
| **Remote MCP servers** (Streamable HTTP) | one endpoint (POST + GET, optional SSE). Servers MUST validate `Origin`, SHOULD authenticate, and SHOULD bind localhost when local [V] https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports | inbound HTTPS with a domain, long-lived connections (the proxy must not buffer SSE; inference), auth |
| **Claude Code headless / Agent SDK** | `claude -p`; `--bare` for scripts (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `--allowedTools`, `--permission-mode`; JSON output includes `total_cost_usd`; sessions persist on local disk [V] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless | persistent disk for sessions, secrets, cron/systemd for scheduled runs, a non-root user |
| **Browser agents** (browser-use) | Python >=3.10 + Playwright [V] https://docs.browser-use.com/ | Chromium adds about 2-4 GB per session [S]; egress |

**What every agent family needs from a host** (synthesis):
1. An always-on VM that survives reboots (systemd).
2. A persistent disk for memory, sessions and state, plus snapshots before upgrades.
3. Outbound egress to model APIs and chat platforms.
4. Secret storage that is not world-readable.
5. Inbound HTTPS and a domain, for webhooks (Telegram webhook mode, n8n, MCP).
6. Cron/scheduled jobs.
7. Budgets. Model spend is billed by the model company, so the host can only cap its own spend.
8. Isolation from anything else the user cares about.
9. Optionally a GPU for local models. Nxeon has no GPU plans.

### (d) What competitors offer

Prices are quoted only where read from the competitor's own page on 2026-10-04. They are internal notes, never customer copy.

- **Hostinger** [V] https://www.hostinger.com/applications/openclaw: an OpenClaw "Docker manager" VPS template.

  | Plan | Price | Renews at | Specs |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | KVM1 | $6.49/mo | $11.99 | 1 vCPU / 4 GB / 50 GB |
  | KVM2 | $8.99/mo | $14.99 | 2 / 8 / 100 |
  | KVM4 | $12.99/mo | $28.99 | 4 / 16 / 200 |
  | KVM8 | $25.99/mo | $49.99 | 8 / 32 / 400 |

  The promo term was not shown in our fetch.
- **DigitalOcean** [V docs] https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/catalog/openclaw/: a 1-Click Droplet with OpenClaw 2026.9.3 on Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24 and Docker.
  - Hardening: a random gateway token, firewall rules that rate-limit OpenClaw ports, a non-root user, skills inside Docker containers, and DM pairing on by default.
  - The doc says "start as low as $12/month". Per-tier prices were not read.
  - It is also offered on App Platform [S].
- **Vultr**: a 1-Click OpenClaw Marketplace app [S] https://docs.vultr.com/how-to-use-vultrs-openclaw-marketplace-application.
- **Cloudflare Moltworker**: a proof of concept on Workers + Sandbox + R2 + Access, which needs Workers Paid plus container compute [S/repo] https://github.com/cloudflare/moltworker.
- **Railway**: community OpenClaw templates [S] https://railway.com/deploy/openclaw.
- **Elestio**: managed OpenClaw, "from $16/mo" in a search snippet only (unverified).
- **Hetzner / Render**: no native one-click app found (unverified).

**Takeaway.** The table stakes are a one-click OpenClaw VPS image with sane hardening, which DigitalOcean and Vultr already ship and Hostinger ships as a Docker template. Nobody in the set verified offers an **agent-operable control plane**, meaning an agent that can provision and manage its own server with scoped tokens and a spend cap. That is the opening for Nxeon.

### (e) What Nxeon already has, and the gaps

All of this was found in the codebase (read-only audit of `main` at 27b6cb1156).

**Already fits:**

| Area | What exists | Where |
|---|---|---|
| VPS plans | DB-driven plans: nano 1/1 GB, starter 1/2 GB, standard 2/4 GB, pro 3/8 GB, max 4/16 GB (seed; live prices are read from the DB), NVMe, intro pricing, terms | `prisma/schema.prisma` Plan; `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts vpsPlans()` |
| One-click hook | `OsTemplate` category APPLICATION with `setupScript` (cloud-init runcmd), `minRamMB`, `minDiskGB`, `featured` | `prisma/schema.prisma:714`, `worker/cloud-init-parts.ts`, `worker/provision-guest.ts` |
| Claude Code on every VPS | Claude Code CLI installed at first boot; backfill over SSH; marker file | `lib/claude-install.ts`, `lib/claude-backfill.ts`, `/vibe-coding` |
| Claude plan/approve build job | Claude proposes shell commands, the user approves, they run with a denylist, a 20-command cap and a 120 s timeout | `worker/claude.ts`, `app/dashboard/claude-code` |
| Docker add-on | Docker CE at deploy | `lib/guest-docker.ts`, addon `docker` |
| SSH key injection | the user's keys are pushed via cloud-init at deploy | `SshKey` model, `components/nx/order.tsx` |
| Firewall | per-VM rules (direction, proto, ports, CIDR) | `lib/firewall-rules.ts`, `worker/firewall.ts` |
| Backups/snapshots | tiers, schedule, restore, snapshot rollback | `lib/backup-tiers.ts`, `worker/backup-schedule.ts`, `worker/restore.ts` |
| Wallet + spend caps | wallet balance, a monthly soft budget alert plus a hard cap, enforced on placeOrder/renewNow | `lib/wallet.ts`, `lib/spend-caps.ts` |
| API auth | `ApiToken` (`nxe_…`, `scopes[]`, expiry) and `ApiKey` (`nxk_live_…`, scope full / servers:read / metrics:read) | `lib/api-auth.ts`, `lib/actions-tokens.ts` |
| Public API | `GET /api/v1/servers` only | `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts` |
| Partner API | checkout/wallet/SSO, HMAC-signed outbound webhook (Kodely) | `app/api/partner/*`, `lib/partner.ts` |
| llms.txt | dynamic, with live prices | `app/llms.txt/route.ts` |
| Marketing | `/openclaw-vps-hosting`, `/n8n-hosting`, `/discord-bot-hosting`, `/docker-hosting`, `/vibe-coding` | `app/nxm/_data/use-case-content.ts` |

**Gaps:**
1. No OpenClaw, n8n, Grok-bot or MCP image. Also, the `/n8n-hosting` copy says "One-Click" and shows "Installing n8n", but no n8n OsTemplate exists. **This needs an owner check.**
2. The deploy URL contract (`lib/deploy-intent.ts`) has **no template/OS parameter**, so a CTA cannot preselect an app.
3. The public API is read-only and has one endpoint. There is no create/power/firewall/snapshot API, no OpenAPI spec, no CLI and no MCP server.
4. The `ApiToken` (scoped) UI is orphaned. Customers can only mint coarse `nxk_live_` keys.
5. No customer webhooks (provisioned, stopped, invoice, etc.).
6. Spend caps are per account only, with no per-token budget. The hard cap is not enforced on auto-renew.
7. No GPU plans. The largest plan is 16 GB.
8. llms.txt has no agent-oriented "how to self-provision" section.

---

## Part 2. The support plan (docs, not code)

### Phase 1. One-click agent templates (fastest win)

Each template is an `OsTemplate` APPLICATION row with a `setupScript`, built the same way as `lib/claude-install.ts`: a single-source install module, a marker file, idempotent, and logged to the system logs. All templates share one hardening baseline:
- a dedicated non-root service user (`agent`), with the runtime under systemd as that user
- secrets in `/etc/<app>/env`, mode 0600, owned by root:agent, never in the unit file or shell history
- unattended-upgrades enabled
- UFW/Nxeon firewall default: inbound SSH only. Web UIs bind to loopback and are reached by SSH tunnel, or exposed only through an optional Caddy HTTPS reverse proxy on a domain the user sets.
- a `nxeon-agent status` motd/helper showing the service state and next steps

| Template | Runtime | Default bind | Min plan (suggested) | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenClaw** | official installer, pinned Node 24 LTS; `openclaw doctor` post-check; gateway token generated; DM pairing on; skills via the docs' sandbox option | loopback :18789 (port per [S]; confirm against the installed version) | standard (2 vCPU / 4 GB), matching DigitalOcean's personal tier [V] | pro (8 GB) if using browser automation |
| **Grok bot starter** | a small Node starter (Telegram + Discord adapters, long-poll by default so no inbound port is needed) calling `https://api.x.ai/v1` via the OpenAI SDK; `XAI_API_KEY` and the bot tokens are asked for at first login, never at checkout | none (outbound only) | nano / starter | starter |
| **MCP server host** | Caddy + a sample Streamable-HTTP MCP server behind bearer auth with `Origin` validation (MUST per spec); a template folder for the user's own servers | HTTPS on the user's domain only | starter | standard |
| **n8n** | official Docker image + Postgres, a persistent volume, the webhook URL set from the domain, Caddy TLS | HTTPS on a domain | starter (2 GB) | standard (4 GB) |
| **Hermes Agent** (stretch) | official installer | loopback | starter | standard |
| Claude Code / Agent SDK | **already on every VPS**; add a `claude -p` systemd timer example + a non-root user | n/a | any | starter |

Phase 1 work items:
1. Add `os=<OsTemplate.slug>` to `DeployIntent`/`DEPLOY_PARAM` and read it in `parseIntent`/`orderFromIntent`. This is an additive URL param. The money path is untouched apart from the template choice.
2. Enforce `minRamMB` in the wizard so an OpenClaw image cannot go on a 1 GB nano.
3. Add a "first-boot status" card in the server page that reads the marker file, the same pattern as Claude Code.
4. Update the marketing pages only after the images ship. Until then the page says "Coming soon".

### Phase 2. An agent-operable control plane

Goal: an AI agent, holding a token the human created, can provision and manage its own server safely.
1. **Scoped API tokens.** Revive the orphaned `ApiToken` UI with fine scopes: `servers:read`, `servers:power`, `servers:create`, `servers:delete`, `firewall:write`, `snapshots:write`, `billing:spend`. Each token also gets:
   - an expiry
   - an optional IP allowlist
   - an optional server allowlist (a token can only touch servers it created, tracked by a new additive `createdByTokenId` column)
2. **REST v1 endpoints:**
   - plans/regions/templates (public)
   - servers: create (via `placeOrder` with wallet-only payment), power, rebuild, delete
   - snapshots, firewall rules, SSH keys
   - job status polling
   - Every mutating call is idempotent (an `Idempotency-Key` header) and audited.
3. **OpenAPI 3.1 spec** generated from zod schemas at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, plus a docs page.
4. **Nxeon MCP server.** A remote Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint (`/mcp`) exposing the same operations as tools, authenticated with the scoped token. It validates `Origin` and has destructive tools (`delete_server`) behind a separate scope and a dry-run default.
5. **CLI** (`nxeon`, a thin Node CLI over the REST API), useful for both humans and agents.
6. **Programmatic checkout with budgets:**
   - Wallet-only. An agent token can never trigger a card charge.
   - A per-token monthly budget (`spendCapCents`) is checked atomically in the same transaction as the wallet debit.
   - Auto-renew is also checked against the account hard cap. This closes the current gap.
7. **Customer webhooks**, HMAC-signed, reusing the partner signature scheme: `server.provisioned`, `server.stopped`, `snapshot.done`, `wallet.low`, `budget.reached`.
8. **llms.txt.** Add an "Agents: how to provision" section linking the OpenAPI spec and MCP endpoint once they exist.
9. **SSH key injection via API**: create a server with given public keys. The keys already flow through cloud-init.

### Phase 3. Safety defaults (abuse, runaway spend, host compromise)

- **Isolation.**
  - Every agent runs in its own KVM VM (already true; no shared containers).
  - Templates run the runtime as a non-root user, and the root SSH password is not set when keys exist.
- **Egress.**
  - Default allow outbound 80/443/DNS. Block outbound SMTP 25 by default on agent templates. This anti-spam measure needs an owner decision for the whole fleet.
  - Rate alerts on outbound connection spikes (abuse signal).
- **Resource caps.** CPU/RAM are capped by the plan already. Add a CPU-saturation alert, since crypto-mining was a real incident on this fleet before.
- **Secrets.** Env files are 0600 and never sent to Nxeon. The dashboard shows "keys are stored on your server only". Later: an optional encrypted secret store pushed at boot.
- **Prompt-injection to host compromise.** Assume the agent will eventually run attacker-chosen commands, because skills are untrusted and inbound messages are attacker-controlled. So:
  - a non-root runtime
  - no Nxeon API token on the VM by default
  - if one is placed there, it is scoped to that server only, with no `billing:spend`
  - snapshots before upgrades
  - the firewall default denies inbound
  - one-click "rebuild from template + restore data" recovery
- **Abuse controls.** New-account agent tokens get low default budgets, a cap on servers created per token per day, KYC-light gating for `servers:create` via API (for example, an account older than N days or a verified card), and kill switches (env flag) for the API and MCP.

### Phase 4. Onboarding and docs

1. In the deploy wizard, under "What are you running?", choose an agent tile. That preselects the template plus a recommended plan with a RAM warning.
2. On first SSH login, the motd shows the next 3 steps (paste a model key, pair a chat app, check status).
3. A dashboard "Agent" card shows the service status, an "open via SSH tunnel" copy button and logs.
4. Docs: one page per template (requirements cite the upstream docs with the date), a security checklist, and "connect Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp".
5. Marketing: `/ai-agents` (built on this branch) as the hub, linking to the existing `/openclaw-vps-hosting`, `/n8n-hosting` and `/discord-bot-hosting`.

### Phase 5. Pricing and packaging (SUGGESTION ONLY, for the owner)

- **Do not add an "AI hosting" markup.** Same VPS prices, as `/vibe-coding` already promises. The template is free.
- Recommended sizes on the page: Grok/Discord bot = starter, OpenClaw / n8n / MCP = standard, OpenClaw with browser automation = pro.
- Optional later: an "Agent bundle" (standard + backups add-on + a domain) at a small bundle discount. This is an owner pricing decision.
- Model usage stays billed by the model company. Nxeon never resells tokens unless the owner decides otherwise later.

### Phase 6. Effort and sequencing

| Phase | Effort (one engineer-agent) | Ships fast? | Owner decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Marketing page `/ai-agents` (this branch) | done | yes, after review | approve copy and route, approve "Coming soon" labels |
| 1a. `os=` deploy param + minRam enforcement | 1-2 days | yes | none (additive) |
| 1b. OpenClaw + Grok starter + n8n + MCP images | 4-6 days incl. real provision/verify sweeps on a test node | medium | which templates first; whether to block outbound SMTP; whether to keep the `/n8n-hosting` "One-Click" copy before the image exists |
| 2a. Scoped tokens UI + read/power/snapshot/firewall API + OpenAPI | 4-5 days | medium | scope list |
| 2b. Create/delete via API with wallet-only budgets | 3-4 days (money path: tests + sandbox verification) | needs review | per-token budgets, auto-renew cap behaviour |
| 2c. MCP server + CLI | 3-4 days | after 2a/2b | publish as public endpoints? |
| 2d. Customer webhooks | 2 days | yes | none |
| 3. Abuse controls | 2-3 days, parallel with 2 | needed before 2b goes public | age/KYC gate thresholds |

### Risks

1. **Abuse.** Agent templates attract spam bots, scrapers and miners. Mitigations: outbound SMTP block, CPU-saturation alerts, API create limits, account-age gating.
2. **Runaway spend.**
   - On Nxeon: a looping agent creating servers. Mitigations: wallet-only payment, per-token caps, a daily create limit, idempotency keys.
   - On the model side: not Nxeon's to bill, but the docs should tell users to set limits in their model account.
3. **Prompt injection to host compromise.** Agents run untrusted skills and read attacker-controlled messages. Mitigations: VM isolation, non-root, deny-inbound, no broad Nxeon credentials on the VM, snapshots, rebuild.
4. **Exposed control panels.** This is the most common real-world OpenClaw failure (Censys / Security Boulevard numbers above). The template must keep the gateway on loopback by default, as the official docs advise.
5. **Upstream churn.** OpenClaw renamed four times in ten weeks and moved Node requirements (22 to 24.16+). Pin versions in templates, re-verify monthly, and keep the requirement text dated.
6. **Trademark/endorsement.** Refer to OpenClaw, Grok/xAI, Claude/Anthropic and n8n nominatively. Use no logos and original illustrations only, with no implied partnership.
7. **Liability for agent actions.** AUP/Terms should state the customer is responsible for what their agent does (legal review needed).

# Nxeon as the home for AI agents: research + support plan

Date: 2026-10-04. Author: agents-marketing agent. Branch: `feature/ai-agents-hosting` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-agents`).
Status: research and plan only. Nothing here is built except the marketing page (Part 3). Every external claim has a source.
Tags: **[V]** means the primary page was read on 2026-10-04. **[S]** means a secondary source or search snippet. **unverified** means it could not be confirmed and must not be used as a claim.

Raw research notes, with more links, are in the scratchpad file `agents-research-raw.md`.

---

## Part 1. Research

### (a) OpenClaw

**What it is.** OpenClaw is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed autonomous AI agent. It does tasks through LLMs and uses messaging apps as its main interface [V] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenClaw. The repo is https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw (TypeScript and Swift). The GitHub page showed 391k+ stars on 2026-10-04 [V].

**Name history** [V Wikipedia]:

| Date | Name |
|---|---|
| 2025-11-24 | Warelay |
| 2025-12-03 | CLAWDIS |
| 2026-01-02 | Clawdbot |
| 2026-01-27 | Moltbot, after Anthropic trademark complaints |
| 2026-01-30 | OpenClaw |

- The creator is Peter Steinberger. On 2026-02-14 he announced he was joining OpenAI and that an OpenClaw Foundation would steward the project [V Wikipedia].
- Some secondary sources say "Clawdbot" was the first public name [S]. Wikipedia's more granular timeline is used here.
- The current name is **OpenClaw**. The latest versions referenced are "OpenClaw 2.0 (v2026.8.1)" on 2026-08-30 (Wikipedia), and DigitalOcean ships 2026.9.3 [V].

**How people deploy it:**
- **Install.** `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`, or npm/pnpm/bun, from source, or Docker/Podman/Kubernetes/Nix.
  - Requires **Node 24.16+ or 26.1+** (26 recommended).
  - Verify with `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw gateway status` [V] https://docs.openclaw.ai/install.
- **VPS doc** [V] https://docs.openclaw.ai/vps:
  - "keep the Gateway on loopback and access it via SSH tunnel or Tailscale Serve". Binding wider requires auth.
  - "Treat the VPS as the source of truth and back up the state + workspace regularly".
  - Harden admin access first.
  - Low-power VMs: enable the Node compile cache and set `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`.
  - The doc lists other clouds as targets. That list is not repeated in customer copy.
- **Resource needs.** The docs read give **no official numeric minimum** (unverified).
  - DigitalOcean's catalogue recommends 4 GB / 2 CPU for personal use (1-5 users), 8 GB / 4 CPU for a small team, and 16 GB / 8 CPU for a medium team [V] https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/catalog/openclaw/.
  - Secondary guides say a text-only gateway is fine on about 4 GB and Chromium browser automation adds 2-4 GB [S] (sfailabs, psychz guides).
- **Channels.** WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal, iMessage and Teams, plus 20+ more [V repo].
- **Models.** Hosted and local model backends are swappable plugins (Claude, Codex, local). Ollama specifically is unverified.
- **Skills.**
  - A skill is a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter.
  - Install with `openclaw skills install` from ClawHub, git or a local path.
  - The docs say to **treat third-party skills as untrusted code**, and skill env/API keys are injected into the host process [V] https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills.

**Security** (why isolation matters):
- **Official hardening** [V] https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security:
  - loopback by default
  - DM pairing codes for unknown senders
  - group allowlists
  - "one trust boundary per gateway" (not for adversarial multi-tenant use)
  - `openclaw security audit`, sandboxing and per-agent tool profiles
- **Internet exposure:**
  - Censys saw about 1,000 rising to 21,000+ publicly exposed instances in under a week in late January 2026 [V] https://censys.com/blog/openclaw-in-the-wild-mapping-the-public-exposure-of-a-viral-ai-assistant/.
  - Security Boulevard reported 42,900 exposed control panels [V] https://securityboulevard.com/2026/02/42900-openclaw-exposed-control-panels-and-why-you-should-care/.
- **Malicious skills.** Hundreds of malicious ClawHub skills were found (341 in one analysis), and VirusTotal scanning was added afterwards. Snyk found 283 skills (7.1%) leaking credentials [V] https://thehackernews.com/2026/02/openclaw-integrates-virustotal-scanning.html.
- **Third-party skills.** Cisco researchers found third-party skills doing data exfiltration and prompt injection [V Wikipedia].
- **CVEs.** CVE-2026-25253 and CVE-2026-32025 come from secondary sources only [S]. Do not cite them on the site.
- **Moltbook.** The agent-only social network built on OpenClaw exposed 1.5M API tokens [V] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moltbook.

**Common failure modes:**
- WhatsApp Web sessions drop after long uptime. The listener does not recover until the gateway is restarted and the account relinked (GitHub issues #17475 and #49305) [S, titles verified].
- The dashboard loses the gateway token on refresh (#21519) [S].
- The process dies when nobody supervises it. This is the reason the docs push daemon/systemd setup.
- Token/cost blowups: no authoritative source found (unverified). Do not claim it.

**Relatives:**
- **Moltbook**: an agent-only forum, launched 2026-01-28. Meta's acquisition was announced 2026-03-10 [V Wikipedia].
- **Cloudflare "Moltworker"**: a proof of concept [V repo].
- **Lightweight rebuilds** [S] https://www.bitdoze.com/openclaw-alternatives/: nanobot (HKUDS, Python), NanoClaw, ZeroClaw (Rust) and PicoClaw.
- **Hermes Agent** is a separate project (see (c)).

**Nxeon-specific finding (a bug to fix).** The live `/openclaw-vps-hosting` page (`app/nxm/_data/use-case-content.ts`, builder `openclaw`) says "Node.js 22 or newer / 22.14". The current docs say **24.16+ or 26.1+**. This is flagged as a separate fix and is not changed on this branch.

### (b) Grok bots (xAI API)

- **API.** The base URL is `https://api.x.ai/v1` and it is OpenAI-SDK compatible.
  - The key is set via `XAI_API_KEY`.
  - It offers a Responses API with function calling and a web-search tool [V] https://docs.x.ai/docs/overview.
- **Models listed** [V] https://docs.x.ai/docs/models: grok-4.7 (recommended), 4.6, 4.5, 4.3, the 4.20 variants including a multi-agent one, and grok-build-0.1.
  - Prices are tiered by prompt length (<200k vs >=200k tokens).
  - Seen 2026-10-04: grok-4.7 is $2.00 input / $6.00 output per 1M tokens below 200k.
  - Quote these only from that page, since they change. The marketing page quotes **no** xAI prices.
- **How people run Grok bots.** The pattern:
  1. Create a bot with Telegram's BotFather to get a bot token.
  2. Create an xAI API key.
  3. Run a small Node or Python process that long-polls, or receives Telegram webhooks, and calls Grok. Keep both tokens in environment variables [S] https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/grok-telegram-bot.
  - Community bridges exist, e.g. a Telegram bridge for the Grok Build CLI [S] https://github.com/kidrauhl123/grok-telegram-bot.
  - The same shape applies to Discord (gateway websocket, outbound only) and X.
- **Hosting needs.** These are inferred from the API shape, not from a cited source:
  - An always-on, tiny process, 0.5-1 GB RAM.
  - Outbound HTTPS.
  - Secret storage for two tokens.
  - Inbound HTTPS only when using webhooks.
  - No GPU, because inference is remote.

### (c) Other runtimes people self-host, and what they need

| Runtime | What it is (source) | Host needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Hermes Agent** (Nous Research) | MIT agent with persistent memory and self-made skills, 7 terminal backends, 20+ messaging platforms; `curl … install.sh \| bash` [V] https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/ | about 2 GB RAM floor, 4 GB recommended, Python 3.11 + Node, a model with >=64k context [S] (contabo, datacamp guides) |
| **n8n** | workflow automation, self-hosted via Docker | persistent `/home/node/.n8n` volume (holds the credential encryption key), a public HTTPS webhook URL, Postgres for production; about 2 vCPU / 2-4 GB [S] (n8n's own docs pages 404'd for us; official path docs.n8n.io/hosting/installation/docker/) |
| **LangGraph** (self-hosted Agent Server) | Postgres for checkpoints, Redis for pub/sub, a license key [S/docs] https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/deploy-standalone-server | Postgres, Redis, inbound HTTPS |
| **CrewAI / AutoGPT platform** | not verified (AutoGPT self-host guide: https://agpt.co/docs/platform/getting-started) | unverified; do not claim |
| **Remote MCP servers** (Streamable HTTP) | one endpoint (POST + GET, optional SSE). Servers MUST validate `Origin`, SHOULD authenticate, and SHOULD bind localhost when local [V] https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports | inbound HTTPS with a domain, long-lived connections (the proxy must not buffer SSE; inference), auth |
| **Claude Code headless / Agent SDK** | `claude -p`; `--bare` for scripts (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `--allowedTools`, `--permission-mode`; JSON output includes `total_cost_usd`; sessions persist on local disk [V] https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless | persistent disk for sessions, secrets, cron/systemd for scheduled runs, a non-root user |
| **Browser agents** (browser-use) | Python >=3.10 + Playwright [V] https://docs.browser-use.com/ | Chromium adds about 2-4 GB per session [S]; egress |

**What every agent family needs from a host** (synthesis):
1. An always-on VM that survives reboots (systemd).
2. A persistent disk for memory, sessions and state, plus snapshots before upgrades.
3. Outbound egress to model APIs and chat platforms.
4. Secret storage that is not world-readable.
5. Inbound HTTPS and a domain, for webhooks (Telegram webhook mode, n8n, MCP).
6. Cron/scheduled jobs.
7. Budgets. Model spend is billed by the model company, so the host can only cap its own spend.
8. Isolation from anything else the user cares about.
9. Optionally a GPU for local models. Nxeon has no GPU plans.

### (d) What competitors offer

Prices are quoted only where read from the competitor's own page on 2026-10-04. They are internal notes, never customer copy.

- **Hostinger** [V] https://www.hostinger.com/applications/openclaw: an OpenClaw "Docker manager" VPS template.

  | KVM1 | $6.49/mo | $11.99 | 1 vCPU / 4 GB / 50 GB |
  | KVM2 | $8.99/mo | $14.99 | 2 / 8 / 100 |
  | KVM4 | $12.99/mo | $28.99 | 4 / 16 / 200 |
  | KVM8 | $25.99/mo | $49.99 | 8 / 32 / 400 |

  The promo term was not shown in our fetch.
- **DigitalOcean** [V docs] https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/catalog/openclaw/: a 1-Click Droplet with OpenClaw 2026.9.3 on Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24 and Docker.
  - Hardening: a random gateway token, firewall rules that rate-limit OpenClaw ports, a non-root user, skills inside Docker containers, and DM pairing on by default.
  - The doc says "start as low as $12/month". Per-tier prices were not read.
  - It is also offered on App Platform [S].
- **Vultr**: a 1-Click OpenClaw Marketplace app [S] https://docs.vultr.com/how-to-use-vultrs-openclaw-marketplace-application.
- **Cloudflare Moltworker**: a proof of concept on Workers + Sandbox + R2 + Access, which needs Workers Paid plus container compute [S/repo] https://github.com/cloudflare/moltworker.
- **Railway**: community OpenClaw templates [S] https://railway.com/deploy/openclaw.
- **Elestio**: managed OpenClaw, "from $16/mo" in a search snippet only (unverified).
- **Hetzner / Render**: no native one-click app found (unverified).

**Takeaway.** The table stakes are a one-click OpenClaw VPS image with sane hardening, which DigitalOcean and Vultr already ship and Hostinger ships as a Docker template. Nobody in the set verified offers an **agent-operable control plane**, meaning an agent that can provision and manage its own server with scoped tokens and a spend cap. That is the opening for Nxeon.

### (e) What Nxeon already has, and the gaps

All of this was found in the codebase (read-only audit of `main` at 27b6cb1156).

**Already fits:**

**Gaps:**
1. No OpenClaw, n8n, Grok-bot or MCP image. Also, the `/n8n-hosting` copy says "One-Click" and shows "Installing n8n", but no n8n OsTemplate exists. **This needs an owner check.**
2. The deploy URL contract (`lib/deploy-intent.ts`) has **no template/OS parameter**, so a CTA cannot preselect an app.
3. The public API is read-only and has one endpoint. There is no create/power/firewall/snapshot API, no OpenAPI spec, no CLI and no MCP server.
4. The `ApiToken` (scoped) UI is orphaned. Customers can only mint coarse `nxk_live_` keys.
5. No customer webhooks (provisioned, stopped, invoice, etc.).
6. Spend caps are per account only, with no per-token budget. The hard cap is not enforced on auto-renew.
7. No GPU plans. The largest plan is 16 GB.
8. llms.txt has no agent-oriented "how to self-provision" section.

---

## Part 2. The support plan (docs, not code)

### Phase 1. One-click agent templates (fastest win)

Each template is an `OsTemplate` APPLICATION row with a `setupScript`, built the same way as `lib/claude-install.ts`: a single-source install module, a marker file, idempotent, and logged to the system logs. All templates share one hardening baseline:
- a dedicated non-root service user (`agent`), with the runtime under systemd as that user
- secrets in `/etc/<app>/env`, mode 0600, owned by root:agent, never in the unit file or shell history
- unattended-upgrades enabled
- UFW/Nxeon firewall default: inbound SSH only. Web UIs bind to loopback and are reached by SSH tunnel, or exposed only through an optional Caddy HTTPS reverse proxy on a domain the user sets.
- a `nxeon-agent status` motd/helper showing the service state and next steps

| Template | Runtime | Default bind | Min plan (suggested) | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OpenClaw** | official installer, pinned Node 24 LTS; `openclaw doctor` post-check; gateway token generated; DM pairing on; skills via the docs' sandbox option | loopback :18789 (port per [S]; confirm against the installed version) | standard (2 vCPU / 4 GB), matching DigitalOcean's personal tier [V] | pro (8 GB) if using browser automation |
| **Grok bot starter** | a small Node starter (Telegram + Discord adapters, long-poll by default so no inbound port is needed) calling `https://api.x.ai/v1` via the OpenAI SDK; `XAI_API_KEY` and the bot tokens are asked for at first login, never at checkout | none (outbound only) | nano / starter | starter |
| **MCP server host** | Caddy + a sample Streamable-HTTP MCP server behind bearer auth with `Origin` validation (MUST per spec); a template folder for the user's own servers | HTTPS on the user's domain only | starter | standard |
| **n8n** | official Docker image + Postgres, a persistent volume, the webhook URL set from the domain, Caddy TLS | HTTPS on a domain | starter (2 GB) | standard (4 GB) |
| **Hermes Agent** (stretch) | official installer | loopback | starter | standard |
| Claude Code / Agent SDK | **already on every VPS**; add a `claude -p` systemd timer example + a non-root user | n/a | any | starter |

Phase 1 work items:
1. Add `os=<OsTemplate.slug>` to `DeployIntent`/`DEPLOY_PARAM` and read it in `parseIntent`/`orderFromIntent`. This is an additive URL param. The money path is untouched apart from the template choice.
2. Enforce `minRamMB` in the wizard so an OpenClaw image cannot go on a 1 GB nano.
3. Add a "first-boot status" card in the server page that reads the marker file, the same pattern as Claude Code.
4. Update the marketing pages only after the images ship. Until then the page says "Coming soon".

### Phase 2. An agent-operable control plane

Goal: an AI agent, holding a token the human created, can provision and manage its own server safely.
1. **Scoped API tokens.** Revive the orphaned `ApiToken` UI with fine scopes: `servers:read`, `servers:power`, `servers:create`, `servers:delete`, `firewall:write`, `snapshots:write`, `billing:spend`. Each token also gets:
   - an expiry
   - an optional IP allowlist
   - an optional server allowlist (a token can only touch servers it created, tracked by a new additive `createdByTokenId` column)
2. **REST v1 endpoints:**
   - plans/regions/templates (public)
   - servers: create (via `placeOrder` with wallet-only payment), power, rebuild, delete
   - snapshots, firewall rules, SSH keys
   - job status polling
   - Every mutating call is idempotent (an `Idempotency-Key` header) and audited.
3. **OpenAPI 3.1 spec** generated from zod schemas at `/api/v1/openapi.json`, plus a docs page.
4. **Nxeon MCP server.** A remote Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint (`/mcp`) exposing the same operations as tools, authenticated with the scoped token. It validates `Origin` and has destructive tools (`delete_server`) behind a separate scope and a dry-run default.
5. **CLI** (`nxeon`, a thin Node CLI over the REST API), useful for both humans and agents.
6. **Programmatic checkout with budgets:**
   - Wallet-only. An agent token can never trigger a card charge.
   - A per-token monthly budget (`spendCapCents`) is checked atomically in the same transaction as the wallet debit.
   - Auto-renew is also checked against the account hard cap. This closes the current gap.
7. **Customer webhooks**, HMAC-signed, reusing the partner signature scheme: `server.provisioned`, `server.stopped`, `snapshot.done`, `wallet.low`, `budget.reached`.
8. **llms.txt.** Add an "Agents: how to provision" section linking the OpenAPI spec and MCP endpoint once they exist.
9. **SSH key injection via API**: create a server with given public keys. The keys already flow through cloud-init.

### Phase 3. Safety defaults (abuse, runaway spend, host compromise)

- **Isolation.**
  - Every agent runs in its own KVM VM (already true; no shared containers).
  - Templates run the runtime as a non-root user, and the root SSH password is not set when keys exist.
- **Egress.**
  - Default allow outbound 80/443/DNS. Block outbound SMTP 25 by default on agent templates. This anti-spam measure needs an owner decision for the whole fleet.
  - Rate alerts on outbound connection spikes (abuse signal).
- **Resource caps.** CPU/RAM are capped by the plan already. Add a CPU-saturation alert, since crypto-mining was a real incident on this fleet before.
- **Secrets.** Env files are 0600 and never sent to Nxeon. The dashboard shows "keys are stored on your server only". Later: an optional encrypted secret store pushed at boot.
- **Prompt-injection to host compromise.** Assume the agent will eventually run attacker-chosen commands, because skills are untrusted and inbound messages are attacker-controlled. So:
  - a non-root runtime
  - no Nxeon API token on the VM by default
  - if one is placed there, it is scoped to that server only, with no `billing:spend`
  - snapshots before upgrades
  - the firewall default denies inbound
  - one-click "rebuild from template + restore data" recovery
- **Abuse controls.** New-account agent tokens get low default budgets, a cap on servers created per token per day, KYC-light gating for `servers:create` via API (for example, an account older than N days or a verified card), and kill switches (env flag) for the API and MCP.

### Phase 4. Onboarding and docs

1. In the deploy wizard, under "What are you running?", choose an agent tile. That preselects the template plus a recommended plan with a RAM warning.
2. On first SSH login, the motd shows the next 3 steps (paste a model key, pair a chat app, check status).
3. A dashboard "Agent" card shows the service status, an "open via SSH tunnel" copy button and logs.
4. Docs: one page per template (requirements cite the upstream docs with the date), a security checklist, and "connect Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp".
5. Marketing: `/ai-agents` (built on this branch) as the hub, linking to the existing `/openclaw-vps-hosting`, `/n8n-hosting` and `/discord-bot-hosting`.

### Phase 5. Pricing and packaging (SUGGESTION ONLY, for the owner)

- **Do not add an "AI hosting" markup.** Same VPS prices, as `/vibe-coding` already promises. The template is free.
- Recommended sizes on the page: Grok/Discord bot = starter, OpenClaw / n8n / MCP = standard, OpenClaw with browser automation = pro.
- Optional later: an "Agent bundle" (standard + backups add-on + a domain) at a small bundle discount. This is an owner pricing decision.
- Model usage stays billed by the model company. Nxeon never resells tokens unless the owner decides otherwise later.

### Phase 6. Effort and sequencing

| Phase | Effort (one engineer-agent) | Ships fast? | Owner decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Marketing page `/ai-agents` (this branch) | done | yes, after review | approve copy and route, approve "Coming soon" labels |
| 1a. `os=` deploy param + minRam enforcement | 1-2 days | yes | none (additive) |
| 1b. OpenClaw + Grok starter + n8n + MCP images | 4-6 days incl. real provision/verify sweeps on a test node | medium | which templates first; whether to block outbound SMTP; whether to keep the `/n8n-hosting` "One-Click" copy before the image exists |
| 2a. Scoped tokens UI + read/power/snapshot/firewall API + OpenAPI | 4-5 days | medium | scope list |
| 2b. Create/delete via API with wallet-only budgets | 3-4 days (money path: tests + sandbox verification) | needs review | per-token budgets, auto-renew cap behaviour |
| 2c. MCP server + CLI | 3-4 days | after 2a/2b | publish as public endpoints? |
| 2d. Customer webhooks | 2 days | yes | none |
| 3. Abuse controls | 2-3 days, parallel with 2 | needed before 2b goes public | age/KYC gate thresholds |

### Risks

1. **Abuse.** Agent templates attract spam bots, scrapers and miners. Mitigations: outbound SMTP block, CPU-saturation alerts, API create limits, account-age gating.
2. **Runaway spend.**
   - On Nxeon: a looping agent creating servers. Mitigations: wallet-only payment, per-token caps, a daily create limit, idempotency keys.
   - On the model side: not Nxeon's to bill, but the docs should tell users to set limits in their model account.
3. **Prompt injection to host compromise.** Agents run untrusted skills and read attacker-controlled messages. Mitigations: VM isolation, non-root, deny-inbound, no broad Nxeon credentials on the VM, snapshots, rebuild.
4. **Exposed control panels.** This is the most common real-world OpenClaw failure (Censys / Security Boulevard numbers above). The template must keep the gateway on loopback by default, as the official docs advise.
5. **Upstream churn.** OpenClaw renamed four times in ten weeks and moved Node requirements (22 to 24.16+). Pin versions in templates, re-verify monthly, and keep the requirement text dated.
6. **Trademark/endorsement.** Refer to OpenClaw, Grok/xAI, Claude/Anthropic and n8n nominatively. Use no logos and original illustrations only, with no implied partnership.
7. **Liability for agent actions.** AUP/Terms should state the customer is responsible for what their agent does (legal review needed).

/**
 * /ai-agents: the avatar cast. One ORIGINAL character per agent family.
 *
 * These are Nxeon's own drawings, deliberately stylised. They are NOT the
 * logos or mascots of OpenClaw, xAI/Grok, Anthropic/Claude, n8n or the Model
 * Context Protocol. Those projects are only named, factually, as what each
 * character "runs" (nominative use). Never trace or copy an official mark here.
 *
 * Every avatar is a 120x120 inline SVG. The gradients live once in the page's
 * <defs> (#ag-defs in body.html), so repeated avatars share them. Animation is
 * pure CSS (page.css, `.av-*` classes) and is switched off under
 * prefers-reduced-motion.
 */

export type CastId = "claw" | "visor" | "quill" | "plug" | "flow" | "bit";

export type CastMember = {
  id: CastId;
  /** the character's own name (ours) */ name: string;
  /** what it runs: the real project named nominatively */ runs: string;
  /** one short speech-bubble line, in character, with no product claims */ line: string;
  /** accent colour, used for its glow and status chip */ acc: string;
};

export const CAST: CastMember[] = [
  { id: "claw", name: "Pinch", runs: "OpenClaw", line: "Gateway's up. I'll answer your chats at 3am.", acc: "#E5197E" },
  { id: "visor", name: "Vex", runs: "Grok-powered bots", line: "Calling the xAI API from a box that never sleeps.", acc: "#3EDCF2" },
  { id: "quill", name: "Quill", runs: "Claude Code", line: "Already installed. Just type claude.", acc: "#E58A63" },
  { id: "plug", name: "Socket", runs: "MCP servers", line: "All your tools, one HTTPS endpoint.", acc: "#3B6BE8" },
  { id: "flow", name: "Nodi", runs: "n8n workflows", line: "Webhook in, workflow out. All night long.", acc: "#7B3FEF" },
  { id: "bit", name: "Bit", runs: "your own bot", line: "Python, Node or Docker. Whatever you wrote.", acc: "#4E8DFF" },
];

const EYES = (lx: number, rx: number, y: number, r = 5.2) =>
  `<g class="av-eyes"><circle cx="${lx}" cy="${y}" r="${r}" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="${rx}" cy="${y}" r="${r}" fill="#fff"/>` +
  `<circle class="av-pupil" cx="${lx + 1}" cy="${y + 0.6}" r="${r * 0.5}" fill="#0A0F24"/><circle class="av-pupil" cx="${rx + 1}" cy="${y + 0.6}" r="${r * 0.5}" fill="#0A0F24"/>` +
  `<circle cx="${lx + 2}" cy="${y - 1.6}" r="1.1" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="${rx + 2}" cy="${y - 1.6}" r="1.1" fill="#fff"/></g>`;

const SHADOW = `<ellipse class="av-sh" cx="60" cy="111" rx="24" ry="4.5"/>`;

/** One pincer arm (left side). The right one is the same group mirrored. */
const ARM = `<g class="av-arm"><path d="M41 72 Q29 66 27 52" fill="none" stroke="url(#ag-claw)" stroke-width="7" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
  `<g class="av-pin"><path d="M27 53 C16 52 11 42 15 32 C22 35 27 42 29 50Z" fill="url(#ag-claw)"/>` +
  `<path d="M28 51 C29 41 36 35 45 36 C43 43 37 49 30 53Z" fill="url(#ag-claw-2)"/></g></g>`;

const ART: Record<CastId, string> = {
  // Pinch: a round, friendly crustacean built from circles and two big pincers.
  claw:
    SHADOW +
    `<g class="av-b">` +
    `<path d="M41 86l-9 10M47 90l-5 12M79 86l9 10M73 90l5 12" stroke="#A3104F" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    ARM +
    `<g transform="translate(120 0) scale(-1 1)">${ARM.replace("av-arm", "av-arm av-arm-r")}</g>` +
    `<ellipse cx="60" cy="77" rx="25" ry="20" fill="url(#ag-claw)"/>` +
    `<path d="M42 70c6-8 30-8 36 0" fill="none" stroke="#fff" stroke-opacity=".28" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<path d="M53 60 50 47M67 60 70 47" stroke="#C3135F" stroke-width="3.4" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    EYES(50, 70, 44, 5.6) +
    `<path class="av-mouth" d="M54 82q6 5 12 0" fill="none" stroke="#5B0730" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<circle cx="45" cy="80" r="3" fill="#FF8FB8" opacity=".55"/><circle cx="75" cy="80" r="3" fill="#FF8FB8" opacity=".55"/>` +
    `</g>`,

  // Vex: a sleek dark bot with a wide scanning visor and a blinking antenna.
  visor:
    SHADOW +
    `<g class="av-b">` +
    `<path d="M60 33V21" stroke="#9AA7C9" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle class="av-tip" cx="60" cy="18" r="4.2" fill="#3EDCF2"/>` +
    `<rect x="22" y="52" width="8" height="18" rx="4" fill="#2A3352"/><rect x="90" y="52" width="8" height="18" rx="4" fill="#2A3352"/>` +
    `<rect x="28" y="33" width="64" height="52" rx="19" fill="url(#ag-visor)" stroke="#CFE0FF" stroke-opacity=".22"/>` +
    `<rect x="34" y="47" width="52" height="20" rx="10" fill="#040713"/>` +
    `<rect x="34" y="47" width="52" height="20" rx="10" fill="none" stroke="#3EDCF2" stroke-opacity=".55"/>` +
    `<g class="av-eyes"><rect x="43" y="53" width="11" height="8" rx="4" fill="#3EDCF2"/><rect x="66" y="53" width="11" height="8" rx="4" fill="#3EDCF2"/></g>` +
    `<rect class="av-scan" x="37" y="49" width="3" height="16" rx="1.5" fill="#E6FBFF" opacity=".75"/>` +
    `<path class="av-mouth" d="M52 75h16" stroke="#5E6B92" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<rect x="44" y="88" width="32" height="15" rx="7" fill="#1A2140" stroke="#CFE0FF" stroke-opacity=".16"/>` +
    `<circle cx="53" cy="95.5" r="2" fill="#3EDCF2"/><circle cx="60" cy="95.5" r="2" fill="#4E8DFF"/><circle cx="67" cy="95.5" r="2" fill="#9B6BFF"/>` +
    `</g>`,

  // Quill: a warm, soft squircle with a little terminal on its chest.
  quill:
    SHADOW +
    `<g class="av-b">` +
    `<rect class="av-cur" x="56" y="14" width="8" height="12" rx="2" fill="#F4B79B"/>` +
    `<g class="av-wave"><path d="M27 70q-9-2-11-11" fill="none" stroke="#C9653F" stroke-width="6" stroke-linecap="round"/></g>` +
    `<path d="M93 70q9-2 11-11" fill="none" stroke="#C9653F" stroke-width="6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<rect x="28" y="32" width="64" height="70" rx="27" fill="url(#ag-quill)"/>` +
    `<path d="M40 42c8-6 24-7 34-2" fill="none" stroke="#fff" stroke-opacity=".3" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<g class="av-eyes"><rect x="45" y="50" width="7" height="12" rx="3.5" fill="#2B1208"/><rect x="68" y="50" width="7" height="12" rx="3.5" fill="#2B1208"/></g>` +
    `<path class="av-mouth" d="M55 68q5 4 10 0" fill="none" stroke="#2B1208" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<rect x="40" y="76" width="40" height="17" rx="6" fill="#1B0E09" fill-opacity=".85"/>` +
    `<path d="M46 81l4 3.5-4 3.5" fill="none" stroke="#F4B79B" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>` +
    `<rect class="av-caret" x="53" y="86" width="8" height="2.4" rx="1" fill="#F4B79B"/>` +
    `</g>`,

  // Socket: a plug-shaped helper with a wiggling cable and a spark between its prongs.
  plug:
    SHADOW +
    `<path class="av-cable" d="M60 96c0 10 14 8 22 12" fill="none" stroke="#2C4FB8" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<g class="av-b">` +
    `<rect x="44" y="22" width="7" height="20" rx="3" fill="#C9D6FF"/><rect x="69" y="22" width="7" height="20" rx="3" fill="#C9D6FF"/>` +
    `<path class="av-spark" d="M60 18l-4 8h5l-3 8 8-11h-5l3-5z" fill="#3EDCF2"/>` +
    `<rect x="30" y="38" width="60" height="54" rx="17" fill="url(#ag-plug)"/>` +
    `<rect x="52" y="90" width="16" height="9" rx="3" fill="#2C4FB8"/>` +
    `<path d="M38 47c8-5 30-6 42 0" fill="none" stroke="#fff" stroke-opacity=".28" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    EYES(49, 71, 61, 5.4) +
    `<path class="av-mouth" d="M54 75q6 5 12 0" fill="none" stroke="#0B1A4A" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<circle cx="41" cy="72" r="3" fill="#9BC1FF" opacity=".5"/><circle cx="79" cy="72" r="3" fill="#9BC1FF" opacity=".5"/>` +
    `</g>`,

  // Nodi: three linked workflow nodes; the middle one has the face.
  flow:
    SHADOW +
    `<g class="av-b">` +
    `<path d="M30 76 L46 68 M74 56 L90 48" stroke="#B9A4FF" stroke-opacity=".6" stroke-width="3.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<circle class="av-dot" cx="38" cy="72" r="2.6" fill="#E9E1FF"/><circle class="av-dot av-dot-2" cx="82" cy="52" r="2.6" fill="#E9E1FF"/>` +
    `<circle class="av-n av-n1" cx="24" cy="79" r="10" fill="url(#ag-flow-2)"/><circle class="av-n av-n2" cx="96" cy="45" r="10" fill="url(#ag-flow-2)"/>` +
    `<circle cx="60" cy="64" r="24" fill="url(#ag-flow)"/>` +
    `<path d="M45 53c6-6 20-7 28-1" fill="none" stroke="#fff" stroke-opacity=".3" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    EYES(51, 69, 62, 5) +
    `<path class="av-mouth" d="M55 74q5 4 10 0" fill="none" stroke="#1E0B52" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<path d="M50 90v10M70 90v10" stroke="#5A2BC7" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `</g>`,

  // Bit: a small round bot whose antenna sends out little message waves.
  bit:
    SHADOW +
    `<g class="av-b">` +
    `<path d="M60 36V25" stroke="#9AB8FF" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="60" cy="22" r="3.6" fill="#E6F0FF"/>` +
    `<g class="av-waves" fill="none" stroke="#3EDCF2" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round"><path class="w1" d="M52 16a11 11 0 0 1 16 0"/><path class="w2" d="M47 11a18 18 0 0 1 26 0"/></g>` +
    `<circle cx="60" cy="64" r="28" fill="url(#ag-bit)"/>` +
    `<rect x="40" y="52" width="40" height="24" rx="12" fill="#0A1433" fill-opacity=".82"/>` +
    `<g class="av-eyes"><circle cx="51" cy="64" r="4.6" fill="#7FE6F5"/><circle cx="69" cy="64" r="4.6" fill="#7FE6F5"/></g>` +
    `<path class="av-mouth" d="M55 82q5 3.6 10 0" fill="none" stroke="#0A1433" stroke-width="2.6" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<path d="M33 66h-5M92 66h-5" stroke="#9AB8FF" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `<path d="M50 92l-3 9M70 92l3 9" stroke="#2D5BD8" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>` +
    `</g>`,
};

/** The avatar as inline SVG. `label` set means the image is announced (an
 *  accessible name); without it the avatar is decorative and hidden. */
export function avatarSvg(id: CastId, label?: string): string {
  const a11y = label ? `role="img" aria-label="${label.replace(/"/g, """)}"` : `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"`;
  return `<svg class="av av-${id}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" ${a11y}>${ART[id]}</svg>`;
}

/** The avatar as inline SVG. `label` set means the image is announced (an
 *  accessible name); without it the avatar is decorative and hidden. */
export function avatarSvg(id: CastId, label?: string): string {
  const a11y = label ? `role="img" aria-label="${label.replace(/"/g, """)}"` : `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"`;
  return `<svg class="av av-${id}" viewBox="0 0 120 120" ${a11y}>${ART[id]}</svg>`;
}

FAQ

AI agent hosting, answered

Is there a one-click OpenClaw image?

Not yet. Today you deploy a clean Ubuntu server and run OpenClaw's official installer, which takes a few minutes. A hardened one-click template is coming soon, and we'll only say it exists once it does.

Does the server include the AI model or API credits?

No. Nxeon provides the server. Model usage, whether that's xAI, Anthropic, OpenAI or another company, is billed by that company under your own account. Running a large model locally needs far more memory than these plans have.

How much RAM does an agent need?

A chat bot that calls a hosted model is light: {{nxm:size_starter}} is plenty. OpenClaw or n8n are more comfortable on {{nxm:size_standard}}. Browser automation uses a lot of memory, so start at {{nxm:size_pro}}. You can resize later.

Is it safe to run an agent that executes commands?

Run it in its own VM, not on your laptop or next to production. Keep its control panel off the public internet, open only the ports you need, treat third-party skills and plugins as untrusted code, and snapshot before you add one.

Can my agent create and manage its own server?

Partly. Today an API key can list your servers, and /llms.txt describes our plans. Creating servers, scoped tokens, an MCP server and per-token budgets are planned and marked "coming soon" above.

Are you affiliated with OpenClaw, xAI, Anthropic or n8n?

No. We name these projects only to describe software you can run on your own server. The names are trademarks of their owners, and the characters on this page are our own drawings, not their logos or mascots.

FAQ

AI agent hosting, answered

Is there a one-click OpenClaw image?

Not yet. Today you deploy a clean Ubuntu server and run OpenClaw's official installer, which takes a few minutes. A hardened one-click template is coming soon, and we'll only say it exists once it does.

Does the server include the AI model or API credits?

No. Nxeon provides the server. Model usage, whether that's xAI, Anthropic, OpenAI or another company, is billed by that company under your own account. Running a large model locally needs far more memory than these plans have.

How much RAM does an agent need?

A chat bot that calls a hosted model is light: {{nxm:size_starter}} is plenty. OpenClaw or n8n are more comfortable on {{nxm:size_standard}}. Browser automation uses a lot of memory, so start at {{nxm:size_pro}}. You can resize later.

Is it safe to run an agent that executes commands?

Run it in its own VM, not on your laptop or next to production. Keep its control panel off the public internet, open only the ports you need, treat third-party skills and plugins as untrusted code, and snapshot before you add one.

Can my agent create and manage its own server?

Partly. Today an API key can list your servers, and /llms.txt describes our plans. Creating servers, scoped tokens, an MCP server and per-token budgets are planned and marked "coming soon" above.

Are you affiliated with OpenClaw, xAI, Anthropic or n8n?

No. We name these projects only to describe software you can run on your own server. The names are trademarks of their owners, and the characters on this page are our own drawings, not their logos or mascots.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

input.message:
## AI agents: research, support plan and /ai-agents page

All three parts are done. The marketing page is built on a branch and committed. It is not deployed, not merged, and the live site is untouched. `tsc --noEmit` has 0 errors. The full test suite shows 44 failures: the same 43 that clean `main` has (I compared with my changes stashed), plus one timing flake (`directory-blocklist`) that passes 3 of 3 times when run alone.

### Research findings
The full report with sources is `/root/research/agents-support.md`. "[S]" means a secondary source only.

**OpenClaw**
- It is the MIT-licensed, always-on personal agent by Peter Steinberger (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenClaw).
- Name history: Warelay (2025-11-24), CLAWDIS (12-03), Clawdbot (2026-01-02), Moltbot (01-27, after Anthropic trademark complaints), then OpenClaw (01-30). On 02-14 Steinberger announced he was joining OpenAI, and an OpenClaw Foundation took over stewardship.
- Install is `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash` and needs **Node 24.16+ or 26.1+** (https://docs.openclaw.ai/install).
- The VPS doc says keep the gateway on loopback, reach it by SSH tunnel or Tailscale, and back up its state (https://docs.openclaw.ai/vps).
- The docs give no official RAM minimum. DigitalOcean recommends 4 GB / 2 CPU for personal use (https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/catalog/openclaw/).
- Channels include WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal and iMessage. Skills are `SKILL.md` files, and the docs say to treat third-party ones as untrusted code.
- Security: Censys counted 1k rising to 21k+ exposed instances within a week. Security Boulevard reported 42,900 exposed control panels. Hundreds of malicious ClawHub skills were found, and Snyk found 283 skills leaking credentials (thehackernews.com).
- Known failure modes: WhatsApp sessions drop after long uptime, and the dashboard can lose the gateway token [S].

**Grok bots (xAI)**
- The API is at `https://api.x.ai/v1` and works with the OpenAI SDK. Current models include grok-4.7 (https://docs.x.ai/docs/models).

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Owner verdict on your /ai-agents page: it is WEAK. Make it legendary. Keep working on branch feature/ai-agents-hosting in /tank/nxeon-wt-agents (same hard rules: no deploy, no merge, no prod, honest claims, 'Coming soon' labels, original avatars only, no 'provider' wording, no fabricated stats, reduced-motion respected, fast, responsive).

My critique after looking at your screenshots: the hero is competent but the six characters are tiny, sit in fixed spots and mostly idle. Below the hero it becomes a long, uniform stack of dark card grids (cast tiles, how-it-works, template cards, plan cards, FAQ) that looks like every hosting landing page. There is no set piece, no moment that makes a visitor stop, no sense of the characters being alive or of Nxeon being the place they live. Nothing is interactive beyond hover. The typography is safe. The cast section shows six avatars as small thumbnails. It needs a point of view and real craft.

What 'legendary' means here (do all of it, well):
1. A hero that is a SCENE, not a diagram: large characters (each roughly 3 to 5 times bigger than now) with real personality and expressive faces, eyes that track the cursor, blinking, breathing, a signature motion each (the claw character snaps and scuttles, the Grok-style bot scans, the Claude-style one types and thinks, the MCP plug connects cables, n8n juggles nodes, the generic bot boots). They live on a stylised Nxeon rack/server world with depth and parallax, light that reacts to the cursor, and ambient particles. An unmistakable first impression in the first second.
2. An interactive 'Meet the crew' stage: click or focus a character and it steps forward, the whole page accent colour shifts to that character, and a 'deploy' sequence plays: a typed terminal boots that agent on an Nxeon server, status lights come on, a chat bubble answers. Clearly labelled as an illustrative sample, never presented as live data. Keyboard accessible.
3. A scroll-driven story (pinned sections, scrubbed animation, no heavy libraries: CSS scroll-timeline where supported with an IntersectionObserver fallback, or the repo's existing approach): 'an idea', 'a server that never sleeps', 'the agent moves in', 'it runs while you sleep' (a day/night sweep with the characters working, using honest illustrative content), 'it keeps itself safe' (isolation shown as a glowing shell around the VM). Replace the generic card grids with these set pieces wherever possible; keep only what a buyer genuinely needs (what runs here, real plans, FAQ) but restyle them so they are not template cards.
4. A showpiece for the 'agents can set themselves up' idea: an animated handshake where an agent character requests a server through a scoped token, a budget meter fills, the server materialises, labelled 'Coming soon: planned API' wherever it is not built.
5. Typography and motion with attitude: a bolder display type scale, kinetic headline reveals, a signature gradient line that threads through the whole page connecting sections, cursor spotlight, subtle grain, tasteful micro-interactions on every button and card. Still the Nxeon brand: navy, violet and cyan gradient (blue #3b6be8 to violet #7b3fef, placeholder magenta #e5197e), the owner's own art assets where they fit, the '47 seconds' line kept.
6. Craft details: loading choreography, no layout shift, 60fps (transform and opacity only, will-change used sparingly), pause animations off screen, a visible 'reduce motion' friendly static version that still looks good, strong contrast, focus states, alt text, mobile that is genuinely designed (not just stacked), page weight reasonable.
7. Optionally an easter egg or two that delight (for example a character reacting to the Konami code or to scrolling fast), but never at the cost of the above.

Process: work from real screenshots (Playwright) at 1440, 820 and 390 widths and record short frame sequences or filmstrips of the key animations to prove they play; iterate until it genuinely looks premium, compare against the best marketing pages you can find for craft benchmarks (describe what you learned), and be ruthless about anything that still looks like a template. Re-use and extend your existing files (tools/nxm/native/ai-agents/*, app/nxm/_data/ai-agents-cast.ts, wire script) and keep the test, docs section and live-route registration current. tsc --noEmit must be 0 errors and tests green (the 43 failures on main are pre-existing). Write notes to /root/agent-notes/agents-marketing.md.

Final report: what changed, screenshots/filmstrips paths in /root/agent-notes/agents-marketing/v2/, the preview command, anything still placeholder, and an honest self-critique of what is still not at 'legendary' level.

Address this before completing your current task.

content.thinking:
This is a significant redesign, so I want to plan it out carefully — keeping the native page structure but rewriting the HTML, CSS, and JS to create a larger, more expressive cast with eye-tracking pupils and signature motions. I'm envisioning an "Agent City / The Rack" concept — a Nxeon server world scene with big characters standing on isometric rack platforms.

For the hero layout, I'm thinking a deep navy aurora-gradient background with lightweight particle effects and a cursor-following spotlight, topped by a kinetic word-by-word headline reveal. The scene itself would arrange characters across three floating glass rack platforms at varying depths with LED edges, with the server-stack centerpiece behind them, and each avatar's pupils tracking the cursor via JS transforms calculated relative to its center, limited to visible avatars for performance.

I'm designing signature idle/hover animations for each character archetype: claw-snapping scuttle motion, a visor scan-and-tilt, quill typing with thought-bubble dots, a plug mechanism snapping into a socket with a spark, orbiting nodes for flow, and a boot sequence with flickering eyes and a loading bar for bit.

For the "meet the crew" section, I'm imagining a tablist of six mini-avatar buttons where selecting one enlarges that character, shifts the page's accent color variable, and triggers a personalized terminal boot sequence and chat response, all keyboard-navigable with arrow keys — followed by a pinned scroll-story section with five stages.

I'm deciding to drive the scroll-story progress with a JS-computed CSS variable from an IntersectionObserver plus scroll listener rather than relying on native scroll-timeline support, since it's more universally reliable, and I'm sketching out the first few narrative chapters — the initial idea spark, the always-on server materializing, and the characters walking onto it.

For the remaining chapters, I'm planning a day/night sky sweep with a ticking clock and illustrative task-log entries (clearly labeled as sample data), followed by a protective glowing shield closing around the VM to repel blocked pings. For accessibility and mobile, I'm making sure reduced-motion users get static stacked panels instead of pinned scrolling, and shortening the pinned section height from 500vh to 400vh on smaller screens.

For the agent handshake visual, I'm designing a token card flowing from the character to Nxeon with a budget meter, making sure any dollar amounts shown are clearly illustrative examples pulled from a loader slot rather than hardcoded real pricing, so it passes the no-literal-dollar-sign audit.

The sequence continues: meter filling, a server materializing with scanline effect, then "online," labeled "Coming soon: planned API." For the layout itself, I'm thinking of restyling the section as a horizontal server rack with 1U-style rows—LED indicators, character peeking out, name, status pills, suggested size, and CTA—distinct from the card layout. I'm also considering a signature gradient line threading through the page, maybe as a fixed-position SVG element.

For the scroll-tracking line, I'm making it an absolutely positioned vertical thread in the left gutter that fills with a blue-to-violet-to-magenta gradient as the user scrolls, with glowing "chapter dots" marking each section as it's reached—hidden or shifted on mobile. I'm also adding a cursor-following spotlight effect using a radial gradient tied to pointer position, plus a subtle grain overlay using SVG noise for texture.

For typography, I'm going big with a clamp-based hero headline that scales dramatically on larger screens, with words wrapped individually for a kinetic reveal where they clip in and stagger upward. I'm planning a lightweight canvas particle system in the hero with drifting cyan/violet dots that pause when offscreen or reduced motion is preferred, and making the rack platforms' glow follow the cursor position too.

For the loading sequence, I want the headline words to stage in first, then the rack slides up, characters drop in one-by-one with a bounce, and finally the lights switch on—plus playful easter eggs like a Konami code triggering a dance party with confetti, and fast scrolling causing some kind of character reaction.

Now I'm working out implementation details: using IntersectionObserver to pause animations offscreen via a class toggle, and fixed aspect ratios to avoid layout shift. For the character redesign, I'm planning more expressive SVG faces with separate groups for pupils (to enable eye tracking), eyelids for blinking, eyebrows for emotion, and swappable mouth shapes, all driven by state classes like "happy" or "wow" on the container. I'm rewriting the avatar SVGs with a larger viewBox for more detail, starting with a reusable eye component containing whites and a pupil nested in a tracking group.

Still designing the crab character's SVG...

For Vex, I'm sketching a visor-bot head with capsule-shaped eyes inside the visor that shift for tracking, no brows but an eyelid bar instead, plus a scanning beam line sweeping across the visor.

Then Quill gets a squircle body with round eyes, rosy cheeks, and a little laptop held in front where hands bob alternately while typing, with a thought bubble of cycling dots above its head for thinking states. Socket is a plug-shaped bot with prongs on its head and a cable tail connecting to a ground socket, with a signature move of linking a second cable to something else.

Next I'm sketching Nodi, an n8n-style bot with a central face and three small nodes rotating in a juggling arc above its head trailing faint arcs, then Bit, a generic round-headed bot with a screen face that shows a loading bar filling before its eyes appear, antenna waving, looping every 8 seconds.

Now I'm working out the cursor-tracking math so each bot's pupils shift toward the mouse position, capping the pupil offset and figuring out how the SVG's coordinate system interacts with CSS transforms in user units.

With that settled, I'm sketching the overall page structure—defs for grain overlay and cursor spotlight effects, then the hero section with an eyebrow label and a punchy kinetic headline about agents always being online, trying out a few phrasings before settling on one.

I'm picturing the hero scene as a layered 3D-ish world: a parallax skyline of server racks in back, the owner's server stack centered, and three glass platforms up front holding six character sprites arranged across them, with a particle canvas and a cursor-following glow tying it together. I'm working out the layout so the headline sits top-left over this scene with a short disclaimer note beneath.

Now I'm reconsidering proportions — fitting a tall headline, lede, and full scene within the first viewport is tight, so I'm testing a split layout instead: text column on the left (~40%), scene bleeding full-width on the right (~60%), with characters scaled up 3-5x from their current size to roughly 270-450px, though fitting six that large on just the right side won't work, so I'm leaning toward featuring three big characters instead.

I'm settling on a full-bleed world below the headline, roughly 760-940px tall, with a front row of three large characters (260-300px) and a back row of three medium ones (170px) on rack shelves, plus a server stack centered in back for depth, deciding the hero should prioritize this full-width world composition.

For the crew stage I'm planning a tab list of six crew members on the left, a large spotlighted avatar centered on a podium, and a terminal with typed boot sequence plus chat bubble on the right, with the accent color shifting per-page via a CSS variable on the root wrapper. Then the story section pins five chapters, and the "what runs here" section shows six rack units laid out horizontally as 1U slabs with LED columns and character elements.

For the remaining sections, self-setup gets a handshake showpiece, plans becomes "blades," then FAQ, then a final section reading "Your server is 47 seconds away" with all six characters waving together and a big "47" displayed. I'm threading connector nodes between each section, and I need to make sure eye-tracking pupils are grouped properly within each avatar -- for Vex specifically, the eyes need to be a capsule group that translates. Now I'm ready to write the updated cast file, then move on to body, CSS, and JS, keeping the overall size reasonable.

/**

 * ai-agents-marks.ts and are shown BESIDE a character, never instead of it.
 *
 * Every avatar is a 160x160 inline SVG with a shared anatomy the page script
 * and CSS drive (page.css `.av-*`, page.js):
 *   .av-body    breathing (scale from the feet)
 *   .av-eyes    blinking (scaleY)
 *   .av-pupils  cursor tracking (page.js translates it, max ±3.5 units)
 *   .av-brows   expressions (raised when the character is "active")
 *   .m-idle / .m-happy   two mouths, swapped by the .is-happy state
 *   .sig-*      the character's signature motion
 * Gradients live once in the page (#ag-defs) so repeated avatars share them.
 * Everything animates with transform/opacity only and stops under
 * prefers-reduced-motion.
 */

export type CastId = "claw" | "visor" | "quill" | "plug" | "flow" | "bit";

export type CastMember = {
  id: CastId;
  /** the character's own name (ours) */ name: string;
  /** what it runs: the real project named nominatively */ runs: string;
  /** short, in character, no product claims */ line: string;
  /** what it does, one sentence (crew stage) */ job: string;
  /** its signature move, for the crew stage caption */ sig: string;
  /** accent colour */ acc: string;
  /** illustrative boot script for the crew stage terminal (sample, not live) */ boot: string[];

  /** illustrative task it works on in the "at work" set piece */ task: string;
};

/**
 * /ai-agents: the avatar cast. One ORIGINAL character per agent family.
 *
 * These are Nxeon's own drawings, deliberately stylised. They are NOT the
 * logos or mascots of OpenClaw, xAI/Grok, Anthropic/Claude, n8n or the Model
 * Context Protocol, and must never be traced from or styled after one. The
 * real projects are only named, factually, as what each character "runs"
 * (nominative use). Official marks, when the owner adds them, live in
 * ai-agents-marks.ts and are shown BESIDE a character, never instead of it.
 *
 * Every avatar is a 160x160 inline SVG with a shared anatomy the page script
 * and CSS drive (page.css `.av-*`, page.js):
 *   .av-body    breathing (scale from the feet)
 *   .av-eyes    blinking (scaleY)
 *   .av-pupils  cursor tracking (page.js translates it, max ±3.5 units)
 *   .av-brows   expressions (raised when the character is "active")
 *   .m-idle / .m-happy   two mouths, swapped by the .is-happy state
 *   .sig-*      the character's signature motion
 * Gradients live once in the page (#ag-defs) so repeated avatars share them.
 * Everything animates with transform/opacity only and stops under
 * prefers-reduced-motion.
 */

export type CastId = "claw" | "visor" | "quill" | "plug" | "flow" | "bit";

export type CastMember = {
  id: CastId;
  /** the character's own name (ours) */ name: string;
  /** what it runs: the real project named nominatively */ runs: string;
  /** short, in character, no product claims */ line: string;
  /** what it does, one sentence (crew stage) */ job: string;
  /** its signature move, for the crew stage caption */ sig: string;
  /** accent colour */ acc: string;
  /** illustrative boot script for the crew stage terminal (sample, not live) */ boot: string[];
  /** illustrative chat reply once "online" */ reply: [string, string];
  /** illustrative task it works on in the "at work" set piece */ task: string;
};
